PART 3

破:两大创世神话的解剖(第 2–4 章)

经济学与国家理论各自讲了一个货币起源故事。格雷伯逐一拆解,并说明谬误为何必须存在、由谁受益。

神话一:以物易物 —— 经济学为何离不开一个从未发生的故事

判断:以物易物谬误之所以两百多年颠扑不破,不是因为证据,而是因为它是经济学作为独立学科的存在论前提——只有假定货币、市场、财产先于政府与道德而自发存在,"经济"才配拥有自己的牛顿式定律,"看不见的手"(斯密在《道德情操论》中明言即天意之手)才得以运转。故一切反证都被系统性无视:英尼斯从未被驳倒,只是被忽略。

教科书叙事(凯斯、贝格、斯蒂格利茨诸版本大同小异):想象一个与今日一样、只是没有货币的小镇,亨利有土豆想要鞋,乔舒亚有鞋不要土豆,"需求的双重匹配"失败,于是人们囤积通货、发明货币。格雷伯的反驳分三层。其一,民族志证伪:凡真实存在的以物易物,都发生在陌生人乃至潜在敌人之间——南比克瓦拉人交易前藏起妇孺、互掷武器、以怒吼砍价、从对方手中抢走货物,宴会随时可能翻脸成战争;冈温古人的"迪泽马拉"把交易、音乐、仪式化性交与佯攻打包成节庆游戏("我们不用长矛刺你们,因为已经用阴茎刺过你们");普什图人的 adal-badal 以坑到远方人为荣。欧洲各语言中 barter 一词的本义即"哄骗、敲竹杠"。其二,邻里的真实解法:在小社会里,亨利只需称赞乔舒亚的鞋,鞋就会作为礼物或人情送到——记住谁欠谁一点什么,配以宽泛的"交易等级"(猪≈鞋一档,珠宝另一档),既不需要通货,也不产生精确价格。其三,历史倒置:凡"退回以物易物"的时代(罗马崩溃后、加洛林之后),人们放弃的只是现金而非货币——账目照旧以旧帝国币记;斯密笔下的纽芬兰鳕鱼、苏格兰钉子、弗吉尼亚烟草,经核查全是信用安排(渔民在商人账上记贷、工匠以雇主欠薪的实物付酒账、种植园主立法强迫商人收烟草)。而楔形文字的破译把书面记录史前推三千年,直接看见了铸币之前的完整信贷世界。

最辛辣的注脚来自田野:马达加斯加通灵人匣中的"古代幽灵"卡拉诺罗,被问及古时用什么货币,阴森答道——"什么也没有,我们以物易物,用一种东西换另一种。"斯密的神话已经殖民了幽灵的记忆。这正是谬误的力量:它塑造常识本身。

硬币的两面:商品论与欠条论为何各对一半

凯思·哈特的意象贯穿全书:每枚硬币一面是政治权威的印记(货币=社会关系的信物、欠条),一面是可称量的金属(货币=商品)。信任半径决定哪一面起作用:社区之内几乎任何东西都能当钱(暹罗赌场的陶瓷筹码、白金汉郡店主亨利的皮革代币),越出信任网络则只剩金银(罗马币流到印度中国,只按含金量计值)。用什么当货币,取决于当时当地的政治力量对比:波美拉尼亚自由农迫使领主收鸡蛋鲱鱼抵税,弗吉尼亚种植园主立法让烟草成为法偿。故"国家与市场之战、政府与商人之战,并非人性所固有"——两者是同一枚硬币。

神话二:原始债务 —— 以及尼采实验揭示的更深教训

判断:原始债务论(生而欠神/社会之债,税是分期偿还)是把十九世纪民族国家的"社会"概念倒放回吠陀时代的自造神话;它无法解释古代自由民不纳税、诸王销债不课债的史实。但它的失败暴露出更深的机制:一旦接受"人际关系皆交易"的前提,任何人——从斯密到尼采到梵书注经者——推到底都会得出"存在即负债"。该反省的不是结论,是前提。

尼采在《论道德的谱系》里做的正是这个思想实验:接过斯密"买卖先于一切人类关系"的假设并推到极致——人是"会估价的动物",schuld 兼指债与罪,债主割债户之肉,部落之债累积为祖先之债、神明之债,直到基督教发明那个"自相矛盾的、可怕的权宜之计":上帝为人类欠自己的债牺牲自己,债主出于对债户的爱替债户还债。格雷伯提醒:尼采知道这套假设是疯的——他是在用资产阶级自己的前提吓唬资产阶级。真实的对照来自格陵兰猎人对弗卢岑的训斥:"在这个国家里我们都是人,我们互相帮助,不愿听人道谢……礼物造就奴隶,鞭子造就狗。"平等社会并非不懂计算,而是拒绝以计算为人性根基——选择哪种倾向作文明的地基,才是真正的问题。

对《梵书》"四债"(向神明献祭、向圣人诵经、向祖先生子、向众人待客)的格雷伯式反读由此顺理成章:这些"债"的偿还方式全都是成为对方——生子即成为祖先,待客即成为人类——恰恰证明它们不可能是债;与"一切"(神明已拥有一切、宇宙即万物)讨价还价,前提就荒谬。人的原罪不是还不清宇宙的账,而是妄想自己能与万物分离、与之对价。而"救赎"(redemption)的词源学(padah/goal=赎回抵押的祖田与家人)则显示:先知与《圣经》的道德语汇本身,就是青铜时代债务危机的政治遗迹——尼希米面对"我们的儿女与他们的儿女一般,我们的女儿已有为婢的,但我们无力拯救"的呼号,召集大会攻击贵族、订立禧年律;"不可贪恋邻人的妻子"的原义,是不可把她作为债奴带走;主祷文的原文是"免我们的债,如同我们免了人的债";而"不饶恕人的恶仆"寓言里那笔一万塔连同(≈罗马整个中东行省的税收)的荒诞债务,冷冷暗示着:在把一切化为账目的世界里,宽恕在结构上不可能。

PART 5

人性经济、社会货币与暴力转轨(第 6 章)

传统货币史里"凭空出现的女人"——爱尔兰法典中作为货币单位的女奴——是被抹去的主线。本章重建它。

判断:所谓"原始货币"根本不是我们货币的原始形态——它们几乎从不用于买卖,而用于安排婚姻、认领子嗣、平息世仇、慰藉丧家、赎罪结盟,即创造与重组人的关系,故应称"社会货币",其经济应称"人性经济"。罗斯帕比进一步指出其本质:社会货币不是清偿手段,而是承认某债无法清偿的手段——人的等价物只能是人,一条命只能以另一条命相抵。因此,当这样的经济被卷入商业经济的轨道,把"人不可换物"改写成"人可以换物"的,只能是持续、系统的物理暴力;大西洋奴隶贸易是其种族灭绝级的极端标本,但同一抽取过程与文明本身同龄。

聘礼、血债与人肉债:不可偿性如何被承认、又如何被击穿

聘礼(bridewealth):1926 年国际联盟一度想把非洲"娶亲价"当奴隶制废除;人类学家胜诉的理由是——买牛者对牛无义务而可转卖,娶妻者对妻负有对等义务且不可转卖,聘礼买的从来不是人,而是重排关系(尤其子嗣归属)。蒂夫人把隐含逻辑说破:体面婚姻是姐妹交换,黄铜棒无论付多少都只是维持"总有一天会有一个女人到来"的礼貌虚构,故"这份债永远不可能还清"。斐济人一枚鲸鱼牙齿的含义相同:承认所求之物珍贵到不存在支付形式。

血债与人肉债:莱利人的血债制度以"人质抵押"(pawn)层层转让年轻女性来清算命案与伤害——每一次清算都要求先把一个具体的人从她的生活语境中剥离为通用单位;蒂夫人的梦魇则是 mbatsav 巫团的"人肉债":被喂食人肉者欠下只能以自家亲人偿还的债——这幅噩梦图景把债务逻辑的终点(以人抵账)以恐怖幻想的形式说了出来,而大西洋贸易将让它几近成真。格雷伯强调"暴力"取其字面义:手断骨折、绳索枷锁。巴友柔故事里,深夜假装打妻试探邻居的男人因无人干涉而举家搬走——可接受与不可接受的暴力之分野,正是两性关系的框架;阿奇亚笔下逃跑被鞭打押回、"恨不能早死"的蒂夫女孩,与人类学图表上优美对称的联姻结构,是同一件事的两面:对称的代价由被交换者支付。

奴隶贸易:债务链如何吞噬人性经济

从布里斯托到卡拉巴尔再到克洛斯河上游,是一条完整的债务链:欧洲商人向非洲中间商赊出货物,中间商向内陆放债;阿罗联盟一类组织垄断神谕与"司法",以罚金、伪案、绑架、人质抵押制造源源不断的"债务人"投入链条。其策略后来为一切黑手党所袭用:先释放一个什么都能卖、人命不值钱的无限市场暴力,再以严酷的荣誉法典与"秩序"进场收割——而秩序的核心戒律恰是"还债乃道德之本"。格雷伯特意声明不责难受害者:设想一群携无敌军备与无穷财富的外星人向我们出价每个人类劳工一百万美元——总会有一小撮不择手段者替他们办事。真正的问题是普遍性的:商业经济从人性经济抽取奴隶,已有数千年之久,"它究竟在何种程度上构成了文明本身?"如果我们变成了一个债务社会,那是因为战争、征服与奴隶制的遗产从未真正离开——它仍住在我们关于荣誉、财产乃至自由的最私人概念之中,只是我们再也看不见它。

PART 6

荣誉与降级:当代文明的地基(第 7 章)

奴隶制不仅输送劳力,更铸造概念。父权制、财产权、"自由"——三件现代基石在此获得谱系学解释。

判断:奴隶制=社会性死亡:把人从全部社会关系中剥离的终极形态(瓦菲 1931 年的普查:沦奴之路全球同款——战俘、绑架、抵罪抵债、父卖其子、自卖其身)。荣誉是靠贬损他人才能增殖的"多余尊严",故最受颂扬者与最受贬斥者互为镜像(国王与奴隶都被定义为"没有亲属"的孤绝者)。当商业经济击穿人性经济,三样东西在废墟上结晶:父权制(把女人锁出市场的恐慌反应)、dominium 式财产(对物的绝对权力,原型是主奴关系)、变质的自由(从缔结承诺的能力沦为主人式的为所欲为,进而成为可出售之物)。我们的法权体系"绝大部分最宝贵的权利与自由,是在一个默认我们本不该拥有它们的框架上凿出的一串例外"。

艾奎亚诺悖论与 timē 的分岔

被拐为奴、最终成为废奴领袖的艾奎亚诺,前半生并不反对奴隶制——因为荣誉由他人目光裁定,要赎回被夺走的荣誉,就必须先接受夺走它的那套标准:这是奴隶制最深的暴力,也是"必须用国王的语言与国王辩论"的极端形态。希腊语 timē 的语义分岔浓缩了同一危机:荷马时代它兼指战士荣耀与伤害赔偿,市场化之后同时滑向"价格"(一磅西红柿的 timē)与"对金钱的傲然蔑视"——荣誉究竟是愿意偿付金钱之债,还是根本不把金钱之债当回事?它同时是两者,这个从未解决的危机贯穿地中海文明。

父权制的债务起源:美索不达米亚千年史

PART 7

五千年周期律:信用与金属的大交替(第 8–11 章)

全书的历史脊柱。切换变量是战争:金银可偷、无需信任、没有历史;信用是信任关系本身。

信用/虚拟货币时代:和平网络、宗教权威规制市场、保护债务人的大制度 金属货币时代:战争普遍、军事—铸币—奴隶制复合体、掠夺性借贷失控

机制陈述:金银锭"扮演着毒贩手提箱里无记号钞票的角色——没有历史的物件",谁都收、不问来路、可被抢走;债务却"既是信任的记录,也是信任的关系"。故士兵(手握战利品、四海为家、信用最劣)天然是硬通货的载体;而掠夺性借贷虽然古今皆有,只有在"货币最易兑现"的金属时代才酿成最惨烈的债务危机。奴隶制的兴废与周期严格同步:公元 600 年前后,欧洲、印度、中国的传统奴隶制同时近乎消失——铸币枯竭、信用回归、圣俗权威接管市场的同一场大转换。

美索不达米亚(主案例):神庙—宫殿的行政会计发明记账货币(1 锡克尔银=1 戈大麦,月俸日粮倒推而来);银条封存库房,债务以万物清偿;密封泥板欠条"向持有者兑付",即最早的可转让票据。有息贷款在此诞生——神庙预付货物给远行商队,因官员无法核验商人的沉船、飞蛇与大象故事,遂以固定利率替代分成(希罗多德记波斯人:"耻莫大于说谎,其次是负债——因为负债者必然说谎")。原理一旦外溢即成消费高利贷:歉收之年,抵押链从谷物、羊群一路吃到土地、房屋、儿女、妻子乃至债户本人,债务苦工遍地、农民逃亡沙漠、社会濒于解体。

拉格什王恩美铁纳以"复利计算"向乌玛索赔 4.5 万亿升大麦(其年入的千余倍)作为开战理由——复利已是常识;战胜两年后,他本人宣布全国废债:amargi,"回到母亲身边"——人类语言中第一个"自由"。

PART 8

不确定的时代:1971 年至今(第 12 章)

新的信用货币时代已经开始,但迄今为止,一切都装反了方向。这是全书的当代诊断。

判断:1971 年 8 月 15 日尼克松切断美元与黄金的最后联系,直接动因是越战赤字(1970–72 年间他向印支投下逾四百万吨炸弹)。世界由此重返虚拟货币时代——但按五千年惯例本应出现的"远离战争帝国+建立护债户大制度"并未发生,反而是:新的全球货币比以往任何时候都更牢固地锚定在军事力量上;劳役偿债仍是全球招工的主导原则;史上第一个真正的全球性行政体系(IMF—世行—WTO 及其外围)按"人人必须还债"运转——唯一豁免者是美国财政部自己。赫德森名之曰"债务帝国主义"。它已在承压:2000 年东亚系统性抵制 IMF、2002 年阿根廷违约而未受罚、2008 年美国金融业自身崩塌——连"债务帝国主义能保证稳定"的幌子也被戳破。

机器的构造:美元—国债—军事的三位一体

美元并非政府"随便印"的法币,而是美联储(私有银行财团的公私混合体)货币化国债的产物——英格兰银行 1694 年机制的变体,差别只在美联储"弹指间把钱变出来"。浮动汇率的后果:美国贸易逆差输出的美元,除了购买美国国债别无去处;国债永续展期、从不兑付,叠加低息与贬值,即一种向全球征收的税——铸币税,或按第一章的用语:贡金。国债的主要海外买家始终是美军有效保护下的国家与地区(西德、日、韩、台、海湾);石油唯一以美元计价,由美军保护国沙特、科威特顽固捍卫——2000 年萨达姆改用欧元,随后的轰炸与占领使一切有此念头者不寒而栗。美国军费高于全球其余总和、维持八百个海外基地与"数小时内轰炸地表任一点"的力量投射——正是这种力量让全球货币体系围绕美元组织;而与核威慑同理,它的效力恰在于保持象征性,一旦兑现即开始瓦解。中国的入场则须以长时段读解:自汉代"厚往薄来"的朝贡贸易至郑和宝船,以奢侈品浸润四夷换取名分本是中国的千年策略;冷战期间美国对东亚盟国的优惠贸易不过是借用此策以遏制中国——如今中国持有巨额美债,"完全有理由相信,在中国看来,这是把美国降为传统附庸国的漫长过程的第一步"。达拉斯联储主席在中国到处被托带给伯南克的口信只有一句:"别再凭空造钱来买美国国库券了。"

两轮"容纳的危机":1945–1978 与 1978–2008

周期一 · 凯恩斯共识(1945–1978)

北大西洋白人工人阶级与国家的默契:放弃改造体系的幻想,换取工会、福利与子女的上升通道;生产率与工资同步增长是契约核心。凯恩斯公开承认银行凭空造钱,并主张以渐进降息实现"食利者的安乐死"。此后三十年,一切革命性运动——民权、民族解放、女权——本质上都是要求被纳入这份契约;马丁·路德·金"我有一个梦想"的修辞完全是债务修辞:建国者签发的承付票,对有色公民被退票,"存款不足"。至 1970 年代,体系无力把契约扩展给所有人(它给不了全世界一个密歇根汽车工人的生活),食品骚乱、石油危机、生态末日论齐发——容纳的危机,契约作废。

周期二 · 金融化(1978–2008)

里根—撒切尔宣布旧约作废:人人有政治权利,但政治权利不再有经济内容;生产率与工资脱钩(生产率续涨、工资停滞)。替代方案不是让食利者安乐死,而是让人人成为食利者:401(k)、全民炒房("房子是 ATM 机")、信用卡;1980 年废除联邦高利贷法,黑帮利率(25%–120%)合法化,讨债从打手换成法官与法警。孟加拉式微贷把穷人的"社会资本"(互助网络)兑换成年增 5%–20% 的资本,十年后以自杀潮与暴力收楼收场,与次贷危机难以区分。这一轮同样撞上容纳的危机:让每户都有房子,并不比让每个工人都有养老金更可行——"资本主义不是这样运转的,它本质上是等级制的、排斥性的体系。"2008,泡沫爆炸。

二重神学:供给学派为债权人一侧配备了神学——吉尔德《财富与贫困》宣称向富人供给新造货币是效法上帝的无中生有,"机遇是神性之舟";债务人一侧则领到忏悔电视节目:剪碎信用卡、厉行苦修、"成为一个更难过但更有偿债能力的人"(阿特伍德:"债务是新的脂肪")。格雷伯戳穿其共同前提之伪:美国家庭负债达收入的 130%,但其中挥霍性开支甚微——人们举债主要是为了灾难性医疗、为了上班的车、为了孩子、婚礼、葬礼与情谊,"人们只有筑起债台,才能获得一种超越单纯存活的生活";于是社会交往本身被当成了罪。而穷人"不能延迟满足"的经济学训诫在此失效:女儿一生只有一次五岁,祖父所余只有几年——人际关系无法像消费品那样推迟。

岔口:想象力的军事化与历史的行动者

2008 后的抉择题——谁有权凭空造钱,金融家还是公民?——答案毫无悬念:纳税人替金融家的想象埋单,房贷者被移交给一年前刚收紧的破产法;"大对话"根本没有发生。格雷伯的时代诊断:过去三十年建成了一台制造绝望的庞大官僚机器(军队、监狱、监控、私人安保与宣传引擎),其首要职能是摧毁"资本主义之外尚有道路"的想象——维持这台机器,显然比维持可运转的市场经济更被看重(冷战结束后俄罗斯拆了工厂而保住了强力机关)。深层矛盾由此显形:政治上必须宣布资本主义是唯一可能,而资本主义自身却暗中需要限制自己的未来——否则信用无限、投机疯狂、机器爆炸;两头夹击之下,我们连"另一种安排"都想不出 [此技术记录过长，HTML 中已截断；完整数据仍保留在原始 ZIP 中]

**结构一览**(结论先行,九个部分):

- **PART 0 总纲**——一个反转(信用先于铸币)、一个机制(暴力×量化)、一个周期(信用/金属交替)、一个伦理(债=未完成的交换)压缩在开篇判决框里
- **PART 1 概念枢纽**——16 张承重概念卡,青色为分析工具、陶色为历史机制,每张卡标注该概念在论证中的功能位
- **PART 2 论证主线**——从"欠债还钱"一句话到禧年倡议的七步因果链,是全书自洽性的检验轴
- **PART 3–6**——两大创世神话的解剖(以物易物 / 原始债务)、三原则对照表、人性经济的暴力转轨、荣誉—父权—罗马法三件现代地基的谱系
- **PART 7**——本页视觉签名:五千年周期带,四个时代按真实时长比例分色(青=信用,陶=金属),下接各时代的事件因果条(恩美铁纳 amargi → 轴心复合体 → 无尽藏与交子 → 白银—中国枢纽 → 蒙特苏马赌局)
- **PART 8–9**——1971 后的债务帝国主义、两轮"容纳危机"镜像双栏、二重神学,收于禧年倡议与"债是被数学与暴力腐化的承诺"

检验自洽性的方法写在页脚了:任取一章论断,应能沿七步链上溯至"信用先行"与"暴力×量化"两块基石,下推至"承诺"的结论。

entries.summary:
**Conversation overview**

The session involved extracting the full EPUB text to a working file at `/home/claude/debt_book.md` (approximately 427,000 characters, 5,140 lines), locating all chapter boundaries, and conducting detailed close-reading of chapters 1–10. Chow uploaded an EPUB of Ray Dalio's *债务危机* (Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises, CITIC 2019 edition) and requested a comprehensive single-file HTML knowledge artifact reconstructing the book's core concepts, internal logic, causal chains, and historical case studies. I'm getting a clear overview of the book's structure now. The first part covers the foundational concepts of credit and debt cycles, using concrete examples like the subway analogy to explain the mechanics, then presents a model based on 48 historical cases that distinguishes between deflationary and inflationary debt cycles depending on the foreign exchange debt composition. The framework then breaks down the typical deflationary debt cycle into seven distinct phases, starting with the early golden period through the bubble and peak stages.

The thinking continues through the remaining phases of the deflationary cycle—the depression, harmonious deleveraging, and normalization—while identifying the seven characteristics of bubbles and the four policy levers available to policymakers: fiscal austerity, debt default or restructuring, monetary printing, and wealth redistribution. I'm also mapping out the concept of beautiful deleveraging where nominal growth exceeds nominal interest rates, and distinguishing between three types of monetary policy responses. The inflationary debt cycle follows a different five-stage pattern, with particular attention to currency defense mechanics and the dynamics of how devaluation spirals into inflation and further printing. The section on wartime economics explores how internal and external conflicts interact with debt burdens, and the transition from inflationary depression to hyperinflation reveals the self-reinforcing spiral that eventually requires a new currency. The case studies are beginning with Germany's experience from 1918 to 1924, tracing how war finance and gold suspension led to domestic debt monetization and the subsequent capital flight dynamics.

Now examining Germany's path through the inflation spiral—the Rathenau assassination and foreign capital exit triggering hyperinflation, followed by the Ruhr occupation and the eventual stabilization through the Rentenmark with its seven-point framework addressing reparations, currency issuance limits, and deficit elimination. The US case from 1928 to 1937 shows the tech boom of the twenties, the 1927 rate cut fueling speculation through call loans and margin buying, the subsequent tightening and 1929 crash, then the deflationary depression compounded by protectionism, banking failures, and the gold standard acting as a constraint similar to foreign exchange debt.

Hoover's policy errors—austerity and balanced budget ideology during deflation—gave way to the RFC and proto-QE measures, then Roosevelt's decisive moves in March 1933 with the bank holiday, gold exit, and deposit guarantees enabling a beautiful deleveraging through 1936. But premature tightening in 1935-37 through reserve requirement increases and gold sterilization triggered another recession with a 60% stock decline, forcing a policy reversal before the war shifted everything. The 2007-2011 cycle emerged from the 2001 rate cuts feeding into the 2004-06 housing bubble, where shadow banking mechanisms like repo and securitization masked leverage that pushed debt-to-GDP above 300%, setting up the 2007 peak with subprime deterioration and the Bear Stearns hedge fund collapse.

The 2008 crisis unfolded through a series of emergency interventions—Bear Stearns rescue in March, Fannie and Freddie conservatorship in September, Lehman's collapse without legal authority or buyer, the AIG bailout, money market runs, and TARP's eventual passage—followed by zero rates in December and the first round of quantitative easing starting with $600 billion in mortgage-backed securities purchases. By March 2009, the Fed expanded QE to $1.75 trillion alongside stress tests and mark-to-market relief, creating the conditions for a beautiful deleveraging where nominal growth exceeded nominal rates and government backstopping covered roughly two-thirds of the debt load.

Now moving into 2010 with QE2 while Europe repeats the same policy mistakes from the crisis playbook. I'm laying out the core doctrinal framework: credit simultaneously creates purchasing power and debt, so outcomes depend entirely on productive use; debt cycles follow mechanical sequences where borrowing pulls forward future spending and mean reversion is inevitable; the math on debt crises shows that even substantial loan losses—say 40% on 20% of outstanding debt—translate to manageable annual GDP impacts if debt is denominated in the country's own currency and policymakers retain influence over creditors and debtors; and the long-term debt cycle emerges from successive short-term cycles, each ending with higher debt levels driven by human nature.

The four deleveraging levers—austerity, default, monetary printing, and wealth transfer—must be calibrated so deflationary and inflationary forces balance; beautiful deleveraging happens when nominal growth exceeds nominal interest rates through sufficient stimulus without runaway inflation, and crucially, printing that offsets credit contraction isn't inflationary since spending is what drives prices, not the form of money; the distinction between own-currency debt (deflationary risk) and foreign-currency debt (inflationary risk tied to capital flows) determines which tools work.

Inflationary cycles in emerging markets follow a pattern: capital inflows create self-reinforcing momentum until a sudden stop hits, reserves deplete in months, forcing a sharp devaluation that spikes inflation around 30% for roughly two years before stabilizing once currency returns become attractive again. Hyperinflation emerges from persistent printing to cover external obligations while money flows into real assets and foreign holdings rather than consumption, triggering wage-price spirals that can't be stopped without collapsing liquidity—resolution requires a new hard-backed currency plus fixing the underlying structural problem. War economics compounds these risks through internal political conflict and external rival powers, with the worst outcome being defeat coupled with debt obligations.

Policy management during crises hinges on speed and decisiveness; effective policymakers need both knowledge and authority, though checks and balances often impede rapid response. Protecting systemically important entities and managing deposit insurance priorities becomes critical when banks operating at 12-15x leverage face potential 30% writedowns. Psychology doesn't drive crises—credit supply and demand dynamics proceed regardless of collective memory. Germany's experience shows devaluation drove printing through capital flight, not the reverse, and hyperinflation stemmed from inability to resolve external imbalances. The 1930s turning point came when countries abandoned the gold standard, which had functioned as foreign exchange debt.

The 2008 crisis demonstrated how speed matters—the Fed applied lessons from the 1930s—and how creative use of existing authority (like the ESF for money markets and Section 13(3) lending) filled legal gaps exposed by Lehman's failure. I'm laying out the seven-phase template for deflationary debt cycles, starting with the golden period where debt growth matches income growth, moving into the bubble phase with its characteristic features and self-reinforcing mechanisms.

Now I'm detailing what happens at the peak—how tightening bursts the bubble, yield curves invert, and credit tightens fastest five months before stock market peaks. In the depression phase, I'm examining how zero interest rates disable conventional monetary policy, how bank leverage multipliers of 12-15x become catastrophic when assets decline 30%, and how defaults and credit contraction dominate. Finally, I'm looking at the harmonious deleveraging formula—the balanced approach with typical dosages like printing money at roughly 4% of GDP annually, currency depreciation against gold of around 50%, and fiscal deficits.

For the inflationary debt cycle template, I'm mapping out the five stages with six risk factors, starting from early capital inflows through the bubble phase where foreign investment reaches about 10% of GDP, currency overvaluation hits 15%, and foreign currency debt climbs to 45% of GDP. At the peak, I'm analyzing why defending the currency always fails—the interest rate differential and forward exchange rate mechanics create a whip effect—and why capital controls inevitably break down, typically depleting reserves by 10-20% over roughly six months.

When the currency floats, there's a choice between a one-time devaluation or gradual depreciation, but either way the currency drops 30%, inflation runs 15-30% for about two years, and asset-liability mismatches explode. The normalization phase requires giving currency holders positive real returns while import contraction reverses the current account from minus 6% to plus 2% over eighteen months, with capital flowing back in over four to five years.

Now I'm looking at the transition from inflationary depression to hyperinflation—the core issue is that countries can't fix their external imbalances so they keep printing money to maintain foreign spending. The spiral works like this: each round of printing goes toward real assets and foreign purchases rather than consumption, wages and costs start indexing to inflation, deposit maturities keep shrinking, and they can't stop because halting the printing would collapse commerce. Eventually the currency loses its store-of-value function first, then its medium-of-exchange function, and recovery requires a new currency plus structural reforms to eliminate the underlying imbalances.

In wartime economies, two types of conflict emerge—domestic inequality and left-right divisions alongside international competition between rising and established powers—which fuel populism, authoritarianism, nationalism, and militarism. The worst outcome combines military defeat with massive debt burdens.

Looking at Germany from 1918 to 1924 as the textbook case of inflationary depression taken to its extreme: the war was financed by abandoning the gold standard and issuing domestic debt equal to 130% of GDP, creating a vicious cycle where printing money caused inflation, which pushed real interest rates negative, which made it harder to sell new debt, which forced more printing. The crucial insight is that war financing itself wasn't the direct cause of hyperinflation—it was military defeat that exposed all six risk factors simultaneously. Versailles triggered capital flight as the primary driver, not the other way around; printing money was the symptom, not the disease. From 1920 to 1921 things stabilized temporarily thanks to speculative foreign capital inflows, with the seven largest banks holding a third of their deposits in foreign funds, while global deflation provided a counterweight. The London Ultimatum in 1922 demanded 132 billion gold marks—330% of GDP—and systematically closed off every escape route: austerity was politically impossible, taxes were already maxed out, there were no savings or foreign loans available, and default meant occupation. That left only one option: printing money.

Three events in 1922 shattered the fragile equilibrium—French intransigence, the collapse of a Morgan loan deal, and Rathenau's assassination—triggering a two-thirds withdrawal of foreign capital and unleashing the hyperinflation spiral. The Ruhr occupation in 1923 accelerated the collapse, with the currency losing value so rapidly that people fled into physical assets, and by November 1923 the inflation rate hit 36 billion percent. Stabilization required seven coordinated steps: the Dawes Plan reduced reparations to 1% of GDP, the Rentenmark pegged the currency at a fixed rate, strict monetary limits were imposed, deficit spending stopped, the government slashed payroll by 25% and cut wages by 30% while indexing taxes, credit was tightened through debt revaluation, and foreign reserves were rebuilt through the Dawes loan of 800 million gold marks. A decade later, the Great Depression delivered a second shock that would ultimately pave the way for Hitler.

The 1920s American boom was built on technological innovation—radios and automobiles—but the 1927 rate cut intended to help Europe inflated an enormous asset bubble. Non-bank lenders exploded from 24% to 58% of the lending market, investment trusts were being launched weekly, and margin buying fueled speculation. The critical insight is that the worst debt bubbles don't necessarily show up as commodity inflation but rather as asset price inflation. The tightening that began in 1928 led to the market peak on September 3, 1929, followed by the October crash with its succession of devastating trading days, as the banking system began to seize up.

The initial downturn looked manageable until the Smoot-Hawley tariff triggered retaliatory trade wars, which then cascaded into a banking collapse—the Bank of United States failure being a major shock. The gold standard became a constraint that prevented countries from managing their own currency supplies, creating a global dollar shortage as countries like Germany, Austria, and Britain faced severe currency crises.

Hoover's policy mix made things worse: he insisted on balancing the budget and raising taxes while expecting private bankers to absorb the losses. By 1932, the RFC and proto-quantitative easing measures came too late, and political cycles interrupted any stimulus momentum. Roosevelt's election shifted the political landscape, and his March 1933 bank holiday marked the real turning point—abandoning gold and implementing deposit insurance allowed the economy to finally stabilize and begin deleveraging in a coordinated way.

The 1933-36 recovery combined fiscal stimulus, currency devaluation, and regulatory reforms like deposit insurance and Glass-Steagall. But then in 1935-37, policymakers panicked about excess reserves and doubled reserve requirements while sterilizing gold inflows, which choked off the recovery prematurely.

Now looking at how these mistakes played out: the sterilization and fiscal tightening triggered the 1937-38 recession with stock prices collapsing 60%, forcing another policy reversal. The path to recovery only accelerated once the country moved toward war production, which finally provided the fiscal impulse needed to fully escape the deflationary trap.

sections.text:
The design system Chow established—parchment, teal, terracotta, and Noto Serif SC—is his personal brand applied consistently across work, so it functions as the creative brief itself. Since the principle is to follow the brief's direction exactly when it's pinned down, I'm applying his system faithfully rather than treating it as generic.

Now I'm planning the core visual feature: a set of hand-drawn SVG diagrams showing the debt cycle itself—the archetypal 7-phase curve as the hero piece, a 4-lever balance scale, and an inflationary spiral, all rendered in teal and terracotta over parchment. I'll structure this as a long HTML document built in chunks, starting with the file setup at `/home/claude/debt-crisis/index.html` and copying to the outputs folder. The layout includes a fixed left table of contents for desktop with mobile collapse, a header with the title and positioning, then a "一页看懂" section that presents the whole argument in ~600 characters plus the master causal chain diagram, followed by five chapters covering core concepts, policy tools, the deflationary debt cycle with its SVG visualization, the inflationary cycle with exchange rate dynamics, and hyperinflation mechanics.

The remaining chapters will cover wartime economics, then three historical case studies—Germany 1918–1924, the US 1928–1937, and the US 2007–2011—each with timelines and causal analysis, followed by a validation chapter with 48 case studies comparing good and bad management, a principles summary, and methodological notes. I'll use his convention of leading each section with a 【结论】 statement before the argumentation, and set the color palette with a warm parchment background and deep ink for text.

I need to create two key SVG diagrams: one showing the long-term debt cycle with GDP rising through short cycles to a peak then deleveraging across seven phases, and another mapping the causal chain from credit through spending, income, and collateral back to more credit.

Then I'll build out the remaining diagrams—a balance scale comparing deflationary versus inflationary deleveraging levers, a three-step monetary policy ladder, the inflationary cycle stages with exchange rate mechanics, and a vicious spiral showing capital flight feeding into devaluation and currency depreciation. For the timelines across the three scenarios, I'll use styled HTML components instead of SVG for better density and readability.

I also need to create two comparison tables: one checklist of the seven bubble characteristics and another contrasting deflationary versus inflationary recessions.

Now I'm pulling the specific numbers from the source material—bad loan loss rates around 40%, with bad loans comprising roughly 20% of total lending, which cascades to about 8% of total debt losses, and given total debt at roughly 200% of GDP, that translates to approximately 16% of GDP in losses spread across 15 years or about 1% annually. I'm also noting there are 21 documented deflation cases and 27 inflation cases in the historical record, where recessions are defined by actual GDP contraction.

Looking at the deflation template patterns, the typical cycle spans about 12 years with debt accumulating at 20-25% annually during the bubble phase over roughly 3 years, reaching total debt levels around 300% of GDP at the peak. Credit tightening accelerates fastest about 5 months before the stock market peaks, short-term rates typically top out a few months before equities, and credit problems emerge roughly half a year ahead of the economic peak. During the subsequent depression, stock prices typically fall around 50% in real terms, banks operate with leverage ratios of 12-15 times, creditors at 2 to 1, leading to roughly 30% write-downs on net positions.

For harmonized deleveraging, the typical policy response involves printing money at roughly 4% of GDP annually, initial currency depreciation against gold of about 50%, fiscal deficits expanding to around 6% of GDP, with stimulus typically arriving in the second or third year after the depression begins—by which point equities have already fallen over 50%, economic activity has contracted about 10%, and unemployment sits at 10-15%. Historical data shows the stock market experiences about 6 rebounds of 16-48% during major depressions before the total decline reaches 89%. In terms of creditor protection hierarchy, small depositors are almost always protected (though about 30% of cases see some deposit losses, primarily in foreign currency), while shareholders, subordinated debt holders, and large depositors absorb the losses, with domestic creditors prioritized over foreign ones and international institutions like the IMF and BIS taking top priority. For non-performing assets, roughly 40% of cases transfer them to asset management companies while others remain with the original institutions.

The recovery phase typically involves merging troubled institutions with healthy ones in about 80% of cases, though returning real economic activity to previous peaks takes 5-10 years and stock prices take roughly a decade to recover to prior highs. In inflationary bubble scenarios, foreign capital inflows reach about 10% of GDP, currency overvaluation relative to purchasing power parity sits around 15%, equity markets rally over 20% for consecutive years, debt-to-GDP ratios climb from roughly 125% to 150%, current accounts deteriorate by about 2 percentage points of GDP, and foreign currency debt rises to 35% of total debt and 45% of GDP. When authorities attempt to defend the exchange rate—typically lasting about 6 months—they deplete 10-20% of foreign reserves through interest rate differentials and forward mechanisms that effectively price in monthly depreciation of 5%, equivalent to annualized rates of 80%. As the depression phase begins, real depreciation initially reaches around 30%.

During the acute crisis period, currency losses mount to roughly 30%, foreign reserves deplete another 10%, capital inflows collapse by over 5% of GDP within 12 months while outflows reach 3-5% of GDP, short-term nominal rates spike 20 percentage points, monetary expansion remains limited to 1-2% of GDP, domestic equity markets fall around 50%, debt servicing burdens increase by over 5% of GDP, foreign currency debt rises 20 percentage points relative to GDP, and inflation accelerates to 15-30% and persists at elevated levels for about 2 years. The output gap widens to roughly 8%, with activity bottoming around a year later at approximately negative 4%. Recovery involves import compression that improves the current account by about 8% of GDP, with the current account typically swinging from negative 6% to positive 2% within 18 months post-crisis, imports contracting an average of 10%, equity markets declining over 50%, and short-term rates beginning to decline roughly a year in.

The normalization phase sees inflation returning to pre-crisis levels within 2 years, the exchange rate stabilizing with initial PPP undervaluation around 10%, exports rising 1-2% of GDP, capital reflows occurring over 4-5 years, economic activity returning to trend within 3 years, and income and consumption recovering within 1-2 years. Hyperinflation is defined as prices doubling annually. Looking at Germany's experience, government spending increased 2.5 times between 1914-17, wartime deficits averaged roughly 40% of GDP, monetary supply expanded nearly 300%, and by 1918 domestic debt reached 100 billion marks or about 130% of GDP, with hard currency debt of 5 billion gold marks split between the central bank and private enterprises, representing less than 10% of total debt but exceeding all public gold reserves.

After surrender, capital flight accelerated dramatically—the mark depreciated 30% within months, stock markets fell nearly 50%, mark-denominated debt increased 30%, money supply surged 50%, and inflation hit 30%. The Treaty of Versailles imposed severe territorial and industrial losses, requiring an initial payment of 20 billion marks. Following the treaty signing, the mark collapsed 90% against the dollar between mid-1919 and early 1920, with year-end inflation reaching 140%. By late 1919, inflation approached 200% and the real value of domestic debt had fallen to roughly 25% of its 1918 level. The Erzberger reforms raised income tax to about 60%, property tax to 65%, and shifted direct taxes from 15% to 75% of the total. During 1920-21, industrial production in America and Britain fell 20% and 18.6% respectively, with unemployment reaching 22% and 11.8%.

The Reichsbank's discount rate remained at 5% through 1922 while the deficit hovered around 10% of GDP, yet industrial production surged 75% from 1919-21. Foreign deposits comprised one-third of the seven major banks' holdings. The London Ultimatum demanded 132 billion gold marks—equivalent to 330% of GDP—payable in quarterly installments of roughly 3 billion annually, representing about 10% of GDP or 80% of export revenues. Government revenues would be consumed almost entirely by reparations payments. By 1921, the mark had lost 75% of its value and year-end inflation approached 100%. The cession of Upper Silesia triggered the largest depreciation spike in October. Three major events in 1922 caused two-thirds of foreign deposits to flee; banks operated only three days weekly. The Reichsbank held one-third of circulating commercial paper and increased lending to banks by 1900%. Money supply expanded tenfold, and from August onward prices rose 50% or more monthly. The Ruhr occupation began in January 1923.

By mid-1923, the government was selling 400 million marks daily to peg the currency to the dollar while charging 18% interest rates amid nearly 10,000% inflation. By November 1923, hyperinflation reached 36 billion percent. A month's entire 1913 money supply could barely purchase a kilogram of rye bread. Suicides jumped to 80,000 annually from 1,200 before the war. The Dawes Plan stabilized the situation by reducing 1924-25 reparations to roughly 1% of GNP—a 90% cut from 1923 levels. The Rentenmark was established at a 1:1 trillion exchange rate against paper marks and 4.2:1 against the dollar. The Rentenbank's credit ceiling was set at 2.4 billion marks, backed by 5% of all agricultural and industrial property, with the government immediately receiving 12 billion in loans.

The government revalued debts to 10-15% of their original gold value, then restricted private credit expansion in April 1924. By May, inflation briefly turned negative. Foreign exchange reserves surged from roughly 20 million to nearly 300 million gold marks between November 1923 and January 1924, bolstered by the 800 million gold mark Dawes loan in October. The government cut its workforce by 25% and reduced remaining workers' salaries by 30%, while indexing taxes to inflation—actual tax revenue jumped from 15 million marks in October 1923 to over 300 million by December. Meanwhile, American prosperity during 1928-37 saw radio ownership explode from 60,000 to 7.5 million units, automobile production reach 23 million vehicles by 1929, worker productivity surge 75% between 1922-28, and stock returns exceed 150% from 1922-27.

In spring 1927, the discount rate dropped to 3.5% to help Europe retain gold, then the Fed raised rates 1.5% to 5% between February and July 1928, reaching 6% by August 1929. Stock valuations climbed to 30x earnings, broker branch offices expanded 50% in 1928-29, and call money from non-banks jumped from 24% to 58% of the market. Trust companies were launching nearly five new offerings weekly, accounting for a third of new capital raised. Banks' capital adequacy ratios rose from 14.9% to 17.2%, time deposits from 23.3% to 35.7%, and margin requirements climbed from 10% to 45-50%. The market peaked September 3, 1929 at 381 on the Dow—a level not recovered for 25 years. Black Thursday saw the index drop 33 points intraday to 272 before closing at 299, with bankers' consortium injecting 125 million to stabilize prices. Black Monday fell 13.5%, followed by Black Tuesday's 11.7% decline.

By late November, the index had fallen nearly 50% from its September peak. The Fed cut rates to 3.5% by March 1930 after dropping 2.5% in five months, while two fiscal stimulus bills added roughly 1% of GDP. The Dow recovered to 290 by April 10, but retail sales fell 8% and industrial production dropped 17.6% through year-end. Unemployment surged to around 14% and capacity utilization fell 12 percentage points to 67%. The Smoot-Hawley tariff covered nearly 20,000 goods at roughly 20% rates—despite over 1,000 economists petitioning against it—and the market dropped 7.9% the day before passage. Canada retaliated against 16 American products, corporate profits plummeted 40% in 1930, and the Bank of United States, serving 400,000 depositors, failed on December 11.

The Fed could only lend to member banks, which represented just 35% of all commercial banks. By early 1931, the Times declared the bottom was in, and the Dow had recovered 20% from its February low. American banks and corporations held roughly $1 billion in short-term German debt, equivalent to about 6% of Germany's GDP. Nazi support jumped from under 3% in 1928 to over 18% by September 1930. Austria's Creditanstalt suffered a $20 million loss, Germany's gold reserves fell a third by June with discount rates hitting 15% and mortgage rates at 20%. Stock markets across Europe and America tumbled sharply—Germany down 14.2%, Britain 9.8%, France 6.9%, and the Dow falling 12.3% in April before dropping another 15% in May. Hoover arranged a debt moratorium, with America forgiving $2.45 billion in payments.

The announcement sparked a 12% rally in the Dow, which climbed another 23% by month's end. When Laval sought $1 billion in new loans in August, he was rejected. France began withdrawing gold from Britain, forcing the Bank of England to sell a third of its reserves. The US extended $250 million in loans in early August, followed by joint US-French assistance of $200 million each later that month. By mid-September, Britain's reserves had dwindled to just over £100 million, and the country suspended gold payments. The pound collapsed 30% in three months, falling from 4.86 to 3.70 on the first day and eventually reaching 3.23 by December, while British stocks gained 11% in nominal terms. Other nations followed suit with similar currency devaluations. The Fed raised rates by 2% to defend gold, and by late September, only the Paris exchange remained open across Europe. Britain ended the year by cutting rates 1% to facilitate deleveraging.

In 1931's fourth quarter, the US lost $730 million in gold reserves while currency in circulation increased by $390 million. The following year brought corporate losses of $2.7 billion and over 32,000 bankruptcies with total debt of $928 million. The Reconstruction Finance Corporation was established with $500 million in capital and authority to borrow another $3 billion, distributing $1.3 billion to 5,520 institutions by August. The Banking Act of 1932 introduced proto-quantitative easing measures, with the Fed purchasing nearly $50 million in securities weekly in April, escalating to $100 million by May and reaching $1.5 billion by June. Short-term Treasury yields fell over 2% in the first half, while 10-year yields dropped from 4.3% to below 3.5%. The Dow surged 19.5% to above 80 by February, though it subsequently halved from 88 to 44 between March and May. Gold outflows reached $206 million in June, and in late July, General MacArthur dispersed the Bonus Army veterans.

The Central Republic Bank scandal in July exposed RFC lending practices, causing borrowing to decline. Chicago, Philadelphia, and Boston withdrew from Treasury purchases. The Revenue Act of June 1932 failed to address the deficit problem as fiscal tightening paradoxically accelerated economic contraction faster than deficit reduction. The summer of 1932 saw a rebound with the Dow reaching 80-90 in August and September, roughly double July's lows. Roosevelt's November election victory was decisive—22.8 million votes versus Hoover's 15.8 million—yet income inequality remained severe with the top 10% earning 45% of all income and controlling 85% of wealth while unemployment exceeded 20%. Germany's top 10% earned roughly 40% of income amid unemployment above 25%. By early 1933, Michigan's banks closed on February 14, and in the final two weeks of February, the Federal Reserve faced severe gold outflows.

Roosevelt's bank holiday in early March halted gold exports and triggered the Emergency Banking Act. His fireside chat on March 12 restored confidence, and within days deposits surged by over a billion dollars. Within a month, 90% of member banks had reopened. The stock market surged 15.3% on Wednesday's opening, and after abandoning the gold standard, interest rates fell 1-2% within two weeks. Monetary supply expanded 1.5% over three months, and the Dow climbed nearly 100 points over four months. Leaving the gold standard marked the turning point—all economic indicators bottomed out. The New Deal programs launched in April with the Civilian Conservation Corps enrolling 2.5 million workers over nine years, followed by FERA's $500 million relief allocation in May. GDP didn't return to 1929 levels until 1936.

The administration then implemented a series of structural reforms: the Tennessee Valley Authority in May, the Public Works Administration with $3.3 billion in June, the Securities Act in May, and the abolition of the gold clause in June enabling massive debt restructuring. The Home Owners' Loan Corporation assisted millions between 1933-35, while Glass-Steagall II established the FDIC with a $2,500 deposit insurance limit, Regulation Q, and separated commercial and investment banking. By 1935, housing prices were climbing over 10% annually and excess reserves exceeded $3 billion. However, the Federal Reserve then raised reserve requirements from roughly 8% to 16% across three increases between August 1936 and May 1937, sterilizing about $1.3 billion in gold inflows—equivalent to 1.5% of GDP—which triggered a new contraction in 1937.

The downturn accelerated through fiscal tightening, with federal spending cut by 10% in both 1937 and 1938, the top tax rate raised to 75%, and the budget swinging from a 4% deficit to balance through payroll taxes and spending cuts. Strikes surged 118% with employment in strikes up 136%, while business credit creation fell 2% and household credit dropped 1%, pushing unemployment back to 15%. The stock market bottomed in April 1938 after falling nearly 60% cumulatively, but the Fed reversed course in late 1937 and spring 1938, lowering reserve requirements back to 1936 levels and releasing roughly $750 million in liquidity. Though equities recovered in 1938, they didn't return to 1937 peaks until nearly a decade later at the end of World War II. Now looking at the 2008 crisis for comparison, where interest rates had fallen from 6.5% in 2001 to 1%, and housing prices surged roughly 30% between 2004-06 from their 2000 baseline. 房利美和房地美在2007年底的利润主要来自持有高风险抵押贷款证券，它们的规模相当于贝尔斯登的20倍，持有或担保约5万亿美元的债务。2008年初美联储进行了大幅降息，同时推出退税计划，但瑞银估计抵押贷款证券的总亏损可能达到6000亿美元，随后几个月出现了多起大规模收购和救助。

贝尔斯登拥有庞大的衍生品投资组合和众多交易对手，最终在3月被摩根大通以每股2美元的价格收购，美联储提供了300亿美元的无追索融资。到7月，两房股价在一年内下跌近75%，国会授权了未指明额度的资金支持，9月美联储接管了两房，但随后发现所需资金远超最初承诺的1000亿美元，而雷曼兄弟在9月中旬宣布破产，其资产规模约6000亿美元。

AIG在9月中旬获得850亿美元的救助，涉及85%的股权转让，随后又获得额外的1500亿美元支持，同时美联储动用了约500亿美元的汇率稳定基金为货币市场基金提供担保，高盛和摩根士丹利也转变为银行控股公司。

TARP计划在9月29日遭众议院否决导致标普大跌8.8%，但10月3日通过后，华盛顿互惠银行被摩根大通以19亿美元收购，随后美联储推出一系列流动性工具，10月标普下跌17%创1987年以来最大单月跌幅，但月底反弹，11月底启动QE1计划购买6000亿美元房贷相关债券，将30年房贷利率从6.3%降至5.5%。

进入2009年，失业率飙升，五大金融机构面临危机，财政部推出7870亿美元刺激计划和2750亿美元住房救助，同时美联储进一步扩大QE规模，购买更多MBS和机构债券，收益率大幅下降。

政府还推出PPIP计划吸收问题资产，G20为IMF增资，FASB放宽盯市规则，压力测试显示大多数银行仍需资本补充。下半年开始去杠杆化，同时多德-弗兰克法案、货币基金改革和消费者保护局等监管措施陆续推出。

2010年市场从低点反弹约65%，QE1结束后推出QE2，欧债危机浮现，标普年度回报13%。到2011年中期，实际GDP已恢复到危机前水平，银行压力测试结果与桥水的独立估算基本吻合，财政部长每天都在研读桥水的市场分析报告。

通缩衰退模型显示利率会趋近零，而历史上48个类似案例的平均利率也大幅下降到接近零。政策工具使用频率方面，合并占约80%的案例，资产管理公司干预约40%，资产留在央行资产负债表约60%，存款人蒙受损失的案例占30%。我还想在第三部分加入一份核心术语表，大约15个关键词条。

战争经济时期，军费占GDP的比例和军人占人口的比例平均增长了约5倍，二战期间美国有20%的劳动力参军。现在开始写HTML，分成大约6个部分来构建，需要小心处理引号和转义，避免变量展开问题。

设计系统用纸张色、深纸张色、面板色作为背景，配合深墨色和柔和墨色的文字，加上青绿色和土红色的强调色，还有金色的辅助色。字体选用思源宋体和思源黑体，布局在宽屏上左侧固定目录栏230像素宽，内容区最大宽度约860像素，移动端则改为顶部导航。

Writing design tokens...

每章开头用一个小的债务周期位置指示器来标记该章在整个周期中的位置，这样既能作为视觉标志又能传达信息。每章以【结论】开头，用密集的段落和加粗的关键句来呈现核心观点。

现在我需要组织这个大约35,000到45,000字的中文内容，分成几个主要部分来逐步完成：首先是页头、样式和导航，然后是卷首总览和主要债务链SVG，接着是前两章的概念和工具内容，再是通缩和通胀的周期章节，最后是恶性通胀和其他内容。

后续会依次处理战时经济、德国案例、美国1930年代案例、2008年案例，最后是模型校验、原则总结、术语表和页脚，同时要确保JavaScript的scrollspy功能正常工作。我会小心处理CSS和JavaScript，避免使用反引号来保持heredoc的安全性，并且这个输出是对书籍思想的知识重构和分析，用户拥有原始文件，我的输出是对概念和逻辑的实质性转化和重新组织。

第一章

概念地基：九条公理HOW DALIO THINKS ABOUT CREDIT AND DEBT

达利欧的全部推演建立在九条相互咬合的公理之上。它们的共同气质是把经济学还原为会计恒等式与供求机械：信贷是同时记在两本账上的一笔数字，心理只是放大器而非发动机；因此周期不是占星术，而是"一系列合乎逻辑、以固定模式反复发生的事件"。掌握这九条，后面所有阶段推演与历史因果都只是它们的展开。

信贷同时创造购买力与债务，好坏只看一个判据

信贷是赋予他人购买力、换取其今后偿还该购买力的承诺。它本身既非善也非恶：判断信贷/债务快速增长是好是坏，取决于借款能否用于生产性目的、创造出足以还本付息的收入。能，则资源配置良好，借贷双方共赢；不能，则双方都受损。达利欧特别反对财政保守主义的直觉——对整个社会而言，信贷增长过慢的代价（错失发展机会）与增长过快同样严重，甚至更糟，因为社会决策者拥有个人所不具备的分摊与控制能力。教育、基础设施这类回报体现在"第二层（间接）经济效果"上的投入，常因保守直觉而长期不足。

坏账的真实成本是一道可以算出来的除法题

书中的地铁思想实验：举债十亿建地铁，收入只有预期一半、债务减记50%——这不等于"不该建"，而等于造价高了五亿；摊到二十五年运营期，年成本仅上浮约2%。放大到整个经济体：典型危机中约20%的贷款成为不良、不良贷款的实际损失率约40%，故坏账损失≈总债务的8%；总债务≈GDP的200%，故损失≈GDP的16%；若以十五年为限将其"社会化"，每年仅约GDP的1%——完全可以承受；若不分摊，则无法接受。因此大量举债的真正风险在于：决策者有没有意愿与能力做这道分摊题。这取决于债务计价货币与决策者对债权债务双方的影响力——即卷首的两大条件。

周期是机械的：借钱就是向未来的自己借

一旦借款消费，就启动了一系列"机械性的、可预测的事件"：先借款消费、后紧缩还债，对个人如此，对国家亦然。书中以加入银行与信贷规则的《大富翁》游戏作比：前期"房地产为王"，后期"现金为王"，扩张与萎缩循环往复，为长期大危机创造条件。周期各不相同的只是重现方式与持续时间，逻辑骨架完全一致。依赖举债进行固定资产、房地产与基建投资的经济体（尤其新兴经济体）波动更剧烈——大楼建成之日，就是相关支出归零之时；收入水平上升还会自动侵蚀出口竞争力（日本七十年即为例证）。

短周期叠加成长周期，动力是人性，托底是降息

短债务周期（经济周期）由央行松紧信贷驱动，衰退可用降息化解。但人的本性是爱借钱花钱、不爱还债，于是每个短周期顶部与底部的债务都高于上一轮；央行以循序渐进的降息托住偿债负担（利率下降→资产现值上升→财富效应→月供下降），使债务扩张得以延续数十年。当利率触及0%，这台托底机器熄火，长期债务周期见顶，去杠杆化开始。美国百年间恰好走完两个长周期：1920年代大繁荣→1930年代大萧条；21世纪初繁荣→2008年危机。

货币有两个主人：交换媒介与财富储藏

货币服务两类人：为获得生活必需品而劳动的无产阶级工人，与出借货币使用权换取本息、股权或资产的资本投资者。这两类群体加上制定规则的政府，是债务周期这部剧的全部主角。多数时候借贷交易使双方受益；但当"一个人的金融资产=另一个人的金融负债"这一恒等式中，索取权远超可供兑现的货币时，就必须大规模去杠杆——自由市场信贷体系失灵甚至反噬，央行被迫成为最后贷款人与债务大买家，中央政府被迫重新分配支出与财富。历史上这种根本性失衡多次上演，斗争激烈时贷款本身会被视为罪恶——高利贷之所以被天主教与伊斯兰教定罪，史家认为正源于信用创造带来的这类灾难。

信贷凭空产生，也会凭空消失——去杠杆化不是心理病

刷信用卡的一瞬间，消费者与店主共同凭空创造了一份信贷资产与一份信贷负债；一旦店主怀疑还款，这份"财富"不是转移了，而是彻底消失了。所以"资金只是从高风险资产搬到低风险资产"的说法是错的——大部分被视为资金的东西其实是信贷。达利欧用一个思想实验反驳"萧条是恐惧心理所致"：即使所有人一觉醒来集体失忆，危机依然照常发展，因为债务人需要偿还的债务在算术上就大于他们能获得的资金——去杠杆化的主要驱动力是信贷、资金、商品与服务的供求关系，心理只影响流动性头寸的分布。去杠杆化的本质，是人们发现"自己所谓的财富，大部分不过是他人的付款承诺"。

第三章

通缩性债务周期：七阶段剧本THE ARCHETYPAL DEFLATIONARY DELEVERAGING · 21 CASES

本币债务为主的国家沿七个阶段走完一轮大周期：早期黄金期 → 泡沫 → 顶部 → 萧条 → 和谐的去杠杆化 → 推绳子 → 正常化。全程的转折逻辑：泡沫期债务增速脱离收入增速并自我强化；紧缩（多为央行加息）刺破顶部；利率触0%使常规工具失效、通缩力量（违约＋紧缩）压倒刺激力量而成萧条；直到决策者以足量印钞＋担保＋贬值中和信贷崩溃，切入和谐去杠杆化；再以MP2/MP3对抗"推绳子"，用五到十年回到正常。在整个过程中，央行的系统性盲区只有一个：盯着通胀率与增长率，却不盯债务增长能否创造还债的收入。

① 早期阶段：黄金期

债务增长强劲但不快于收入增长——因为借款被用于能迅速创造收入的活动。债务负担轻、资产负债表健康，私营部门、政府与银行都有加杠杆空间；增长与通胀"不太热也不太冷"。这是判断周期位置的第一把尺子：债务/收入的相对增速。

② 泡沫阶段：自我强化的三重放贷条件

泡沫始于一轮合理的牛市：低利率抬升股与房的吸引力，经济改善、盈利上升、资产负债表变好。随后自我强化开始——贷款人依据三个条件决定放贷额度：借款人的预期收入现金流、净值与抵押品价值、贷款人自身的放贷能力，而在泡沫中这三者同时向好。于是"年收入五万的人每年可借一万、年花六万"，借款支出又抬升整体收入与抵押物价值。价格越涨、信贷标准反而越松（逻辑上本该收紧），因为放贷与借钱买资产都在赚钱；不想错过的新买家涌入；政府的显性或隐性担保火上浇油；不受监管的新型贷款机构（"影子银行"）与金融工程繁荣，各类机构积累四种典型的资产/负债错配：短借长贷、以流动负债持有非流动资产、举债投资高风险债务、借一种货币贷另一种货币。人性随大流、过度外推近期经验——"共识反映在定价里"，人们据此推断好日子会延续。

≈3年
典型泡沫持续时长
20–25%/年
泡沫期债务占GDP之比的年增速
≈300%GDP
泡沫期债务总额的典型峰值水平
7项
识别泡沫的特征清单（见下）
七个特征，多数或全部同时出现即为泡沫

（1）相对传统标准，资产价格偏高；（2）市场预期高价还会快速上涨；（3）普遍的看涨情绪；（4）高杠杆融资买入；（5）买家超长周期提前买入（囤库存、签远期合约）以投机或防涨价；（6）此前从未入市的新买家进场；（7）刺激性货币政策助长泡沫、紧缩性政策刺破泡沫。达利欧同时警告：单一总量指标不足以预测危机——即使全社会债务/收入比很高，只要债务分布均匀就未必成灾；真正要做的是逐一考察关键实体的偿债能力，"平均数会掩盖泡沫"。

货币政策在泡沫中的角色是全书最尖锐的制度批评：央行以通胀与增长为目标，而最严重的债务泡沫恰恰不伴随高通胀，只伴随资产价格通胀（1920年代末的美国、1980年代末的日本、2000年代中期的世界）；于是央行在"数据良好"中纵容以债务购买投资性资产。达利欧的处方：央行应把"保持债务水平的可持续性"纳入目标——"如果助长债务增长的央行不来控制泡沫，还有谁能控制？"

③ 顶部：好到不能再好的那一刻

普遍原则："当市场已经好到不能再好、而所有人都相信它会更好时，顶部就形成了。"顶部多由央行收紧触发（有时因泡沫本身推高了通胀与产能压力，有时因外部紧缩抽走资金），杠杆与价格越高，刺破所需的紧缩越小、破裂的破坏越大。微观顺序高度定型：短端利率上升→收益率曲线走平乃至倒挂→持有现金相对更有吸引力→信贷增速放缓。信贷问题通常比经济周期峰值早约半年出现于最脆弱、泡沫最大的部门；股市见顶前约五个月是信贷收缩最快的时段；短期利率通常在股市见顶前数月达峰。破裂初期最容易被低估的是财富效应——它对增长的影响此时大于货币政策本身：股价先于盈利下跌，投资者误以为便宜而抄底，却没有意识到盈利即将被逆转的循环拖垮。要预判衰退深度，看的不是紧缩的绝对幅度，而是每个部门对紧缩的敏感性与损失的传导机制——又是那句方法论：看单体，不看平均。

④ 萧条阶段：0%地板之下的世界

正常衰退里，货币与偿债需求的失衡可用降息解决（正财富效应＋刺激活动＋减负）。萧条的定义性特征是降息已不可能——利率贴地，而信贷利差走阔使高风险借款人的实际融资成本不降反 [此技术记录过长，HTML 中已截断；完整数据仍保留在原始 ZIP 中]

案例 一

德国 1918–1924：通胀性萧条的极端标本WEIMAR HYPERINFLATION · THE ARCHETYPE PUSHED TO ITS LIMIT

魏玛案例回答两个问题。其一，恶性通胀的真正成因是什么？不是战时印钞——一战各参战国的融资方式与通胀水平大同小异，只有少数国家坠入恶性通胀。真正的成因是战败使德国集齐了第四章的全部六项风险特征，尤其是一笔以硬通货计价、约合GDP 330%、且实际上不可违约的外债（战争赔款）：四条常规出路（削支、增税、借款/储蓄、违约）在政治与现实中逐一被堵死，决策者只剩印钞一途。其二，因果箭头指向哪边？书中最重要的翻案："此时印钞并不是货币贬值的根源，而是货币贬值导致印钞"——先有资本外逃与抛售马克，贬值推高通胀，央行才被迫在"流动性彻底枯竭"与"印钞填空"之间选择后者。这是通胀性萧条的典型发生方式。

1914.7 — 1918.11 · 一战：舞台搭建
退出金本位 · 本币债务融资 · 货币化的第一个恶性循环

开战即挤兑：数周内央行与财政部兑出约1.95亿马克黄金（约占储备10%），1914年7月31日德国暂停纸币兑金，并授权帝国银行以国库券与商业票据为担保发行纸币——到8月底纸马克流通量已增约30%。达利欧就此提炼一般规律：当流通货币远超发行基础的黄金、而投资者又急于兑金时，央行只有紧缩信贷或停兑印钞两条路，且"几乎总是选择暂停兑换并大量印钞，因为紧缩更痛"。战争开支使政府支出/GDP四年间增至2.5倍；增税阻力巨大、国际市场又将德国拒之门外，军费几乎全靠国内发债——到1918年本币债务累计约1000亿马克，≈GDP的130%。决策层清楚本币债务的好处：帝国银行认定敌国的最大弱点恰是不断增加的（对美）外债。

1916年下半年起循环启动：战时通胀（1915年初已超30%）使5%固定利率的战争债券实际利率深负→民众不再认购→帝国银行被迫把赤字货币化→货币化推高通胀→更没人买债。战争期间赤字平均约GDP的40%，货币供应增加近300%。战争最后两年，国内再无人愿收马克，德国开始借入外币：帝国银行与私营企业各欠约25亿金马克——硬通货债务虽不足总债务10%，却已超过全部公共黄金储备。"与本币债务不同，硬通货债务不能通过印钞消化。"帝国银行行长哈芬施泰因的预言："如果我们不能获得大量战争赔款，还债将会非常困难。"

1918.11 — 1920.3 · 《凡尔赛和约》与第一次通胀
资本外逃是第一推动；通胀顺手"清洗"了国内战争债务

投降消息即引发资本外逃：数月内马克兑美元跌约30%、股市近乎腰斩、马克债务增约30%且几乎全部货币化，货币供应+50%、通胀升至30%。1919年6月28日和约条款公布，德国举国震惊：失去12%领土、10%人口、43%生铁与38%钢铁产能；先行支付相当于200亿马克的黄金、商品、船舶与证券；赔款总额留待1921年裁定。签约后马克兑美元在半年内暴跌90%，年底通胀达140%。因果链条清晰：德国人有充分理由预期政府将以重税与没收私产筹措硬通货，于是抛售本币、转移资产；负有外债的债务人抢先偿还外债，使马克充斥外汇市场——贬值进一步自我强化。此时印钞只是央行在"任由流动性与债券市场剧烈紧缩"与"填补空缺"之间的被动选择。

与此同时，贬值与通胀成为一种"没收式征税"的替代品：到1919年底，通胀已把国内战争债务的实际价值压到1918年的约25%。埃茨贝格尔税改（最高所得税近60%、财产税65%，直接税占比从15%提至75%）与之并行。达利欧点出这一阶段的典型抉择：帮看多货币的债权人（紧缩、通缩性衰退），还是帮看空货币的债务人（通胀减债）？经济危机中，政府更可能选择把富人财富重新分配给穷人——因为穷人更苦、且人数更多。凯恩斯的名言为此背书："通胀是不公正的，通缩是不适宜的……或许通缩更不可取。"1920年3月的卡普暴动（右翼政变，被总罢工挫败）预演了另一条规律：去杠杆与萧条的经济困难，会把左翼或右翼民粹与反动领袖送上台。

1920.3 — 1921.5 · 相对稳定：一个由热钱托起的间歇期
"有史以来最大的泡沫"（凯恩斯语）

全球正因美英紧缩而深度收缩（美英工业生产分别-20%、-18.6%），德国却以宽松政策（贴现率维持5%、赤字仍约GDP10%）逆势扩张：1919–21年工业生产+75%——但达利欧提醒这只是"较长萎缩期内的短暂增长期"，绝对水平仍远低于1913年。国内通胀压力被全球通缩对冲，物价1921年初甚至自1914年以来首次停涨。托起这一切的是外国投机资本：世界相信"德国终将复苏、马克终将回升"，从理发师助理到南美小镇居民都在买马克——到1921年，德国七大银行近三分之一的存款来自外国人。达利欧的注脚：从未入市的新买家蜂拥而入，是泡沫的典型迹象；资本流入 [此技术记录过长，HTML 中已截断；完整数据仍保留在原始 ZIP 中]

案例 二

美国 1928–1937：通缩性萧条的完整标本THE GREAT DEPRESSION · DEFLATIONARY DELEVERAGING IN FULL

大萧条是通缩性去杠杆化"最具代表性的案例"，其机理与2008年"大致相同"。案例的四个支点：①泡沫的杠杆藏在银行体系之外（通知放款与投资信托），银行报表在崩盘前夜看上去空前健康；②金本位在功能上等于外币债务，它锁死了美联储的印钞与最后贷款人职能，把一场可控的衰退拖成萧条；③胡佛的政策组合是"新手错误"的标准集合——平衡预算、加税、保护主义、让银行家自食其果；④1933年3月罗斯福切断美元与黄金的联系是唯一的转折点——"正是在这个时候，所有市场和经济数据都在触底"；而1936–37年的过早紧缩，则以一场-60%的股灾示范了退出刺激的代价。全程还铺着一条暗线：萧条→贫富撕裂→民粹与保护主义→战争。

1922 — 1927 · 早期黄金期
科技繁荣：债务与收入齐头并进

收音机保有量六年间从6万台增至750万台；1929年汽车2300万辆、约每五个美国人一辆；工厂工人时产出1922–28年+75%。"繁盛年代"里资本家与工人都获益：企业利润与实际工资（+20%以上）同升、失业新低。1923–26年债务增速与收入增速保持一致——教科书式的周期早期。1922年初至1927年底，股票投资者回报超150%，领涨的是当时的科技双雄：美国无线电与通用汽车。金本位下黄金流入美国；1927年春，为帮英法德止住黄金外流，美联储把贴现率从4%降至3.5%——"这是央行在无意中吹大泡沫的典型方式"：本国增长与通胀无恙，宽松却点燃了以债务购买金融资产的引信。

1927 — 1929 · 泡沫：杠杆搬进影子体系
"新时代"叙事 × 通知放款 × 投资信托

1927–28年股价近乎翻倍、市盈率高达30倍，畅销书宣告"有涨必有跌"的老逻辑已经过时；经纪分支机构两年+50%，"餐桌上、理发店、有轨电车上"人人谈论股票——新买家入场，泡沫特征清单逐项点亮。杠杆的两大新渠道都在受监管银行体系之外：通知放款（每日定价、随时可召回的保证金贷款——短债长投的典型错配；企业闲钱与伦敦香港的资金"汇成一条金河"，美联储体系之外的贷款人占比从1928年初的24%升到1929年10月的58%——这些非银机构一旦缺流动性，美联储无权施救）；投资信托（1929年以每周近五只的速度发行、占新筹资三分之一，杠杆化的信托份额再被保证金杠杆买入——杠杆的平方）。与此同时银行反而"空前健康"：资本充足率从14.9%升至17.2%、定期存款占比上升——达利欧的冷注："银行报表在繁荣期总是好看，只有挤兑与资产跌价才见真章。"美联储的困境同样典型：通胀不高、经济不热，不愿以加息误伤全体借款人，转而用宏观审慎手段（公开信斥责投机性贷款）——收效甚微。"最严重的债务泡沫伴随的不是通胀高企，而是债务推动的资产价格上涨——央行盯着通胀与增长，就会容忍它。"

1928 — 1929.10 · 顶部与崩盘
紧缩刺破：381点，此后二十五年无人再见

1928年2–7月加息1.5%至5%，1929年8月至6%；曲线走平倒挂、流动性下降、现金回报上升——"资金从金融资产撤出"的标准力学。保证金要求从10%提至45–50%。1929年9月3日道指381点见顶——此后25年多无法再现。达利欧强调：没有单一事件刺破泡沫；杠杆买家的仓位已到极限、紧缩改变了杠杆经济学，价格必须以不可持续的加速度上涨才能维持——这本身就是死刑判决。10月19日（周六）大跌引爆追缴保证金的连锁：黑色星期四盘中-33点、银行家池1.25亿美元托市失败；黑色星期一-13.5%（当时史上最大单日跌幅）；黑色星期二再-11.7%，两日-23%，投资信托的杠杆反噬（高盛交易公司单日-42%）。哈里森凌晨三点绕开华盛顿批准注入1亿美元流动性——达利欧借此第一次点出贯穿两个美国案例的制度命题："制衡机制为常态稳定而设，难以应对必须当机立断的危机。"崩盘期间国债与高评级债走强、低评级利差走阔——周期此阶段的典型市场分层。11月中旬道指距峰值已近-50%。

1930 — 1932 · 萧条：每一步都踩在模型的错误清单上
关税战 · 银行倒闭潮 · 金本位的绞索 · 全球美元短缺

1930：年初股市反弹（4月10日道指回到290上方）——"去杠杆早期，投资者与决策者总是低估实体下滑的深度，最初的政策应对总是不足"。下半年经济明显走弱（工业产量5–12月-17.6%、失业率升至14%），此时它更像一场普通衰退。转折性的政策错误是6月的《斯穆特–霍利关税法》：对近两万种进口品加征约20%关税，1028名经济学家联名上书无效，法案通过前一日道指 [此技术记录过长，HTML 中已截断；完整数据仍保留在原始 ZIP 中]

案例 三

美国 2007–2011：管理得最好的一次THE GREAT RECESSION · A WELL-MANAGED DELEVERAGING

2008是与大萧条"机理大致相同"的又一轮长周期终点，差别只在一处：决策者迅速迈出了关键一步。"1930–33年的萧条持续那么久，是因为决策者反应缓慢，而不是因为问题更严重（事实恰恰相反）。"案例的四个支点：①泡沫照例长在监管之外——五条影子渠道为房地产债务输血，资产/负债错配遍布体系；②危机的瓶颈是法律授权而非判断——贝尔斯登可救、雷曼不可救，差别只在"有没有买家＋有没有工具"；③人的因素被抬到与制度同等的高度——保尔森、伯南克、盖特纳的互补与协同，"如果没有这样的精诚合作和聪明才智，我们将遭受需要几十年才能走出的深重灾难"；④QE=以货币创造对冲信贷消灭，政府最终为约三分之二的债务（≈29万亿美元）背书，切入和谐的去杠杆化——通胀始终未至，公理八再获验证。

2001 — 2006 · 播种与泡沫
"黄金期"的体感 × 影子体系的五条输血管

2001年衰退中美联储把利率从6.5%一路降到1%（已逼近0%的地板——长周期后期的记号），衰退短浅，却为泡沫播种。2004–06年是膨胀最快的三年：增长3%–4%、失业4%–5%、通胀2%–3.5%——所有人都觉得"不太热也不太冷"；而债务/GDP年均+12.6%、总债务超GDP的300%。房地产是泡沫的宿主：房价三年约+30%、自2000年+80%以上（一个世纪最快，除战后）；家庭债务/可支配收入从85%升至120%，债务增幅最大的是收入最低的五分之一人群；2005年房屋净值贷款与套现再融资达5000亿（是1998年的六倍）；次贷占到两成市场份额、LTV升至80%、"零收入证明＋诱饵利率"盛行；《时代》封面发问"你的房子会让你变得富有吗"。泡沫七特征逐项点亮，而美联储照例盯着CPI按兵不动——2001年底至2006年初实际短期利率为负，即便2004年起加息，海外资金对美元资产的胃口（经常账户逆差达GDP的6%，中国等顺差国回流购买）也把长端利率按在地上。杠杆的增量在银行体系之外，五条渠道：回购与商业票据（危机前四年经纪商回购负债+2.5倍）、体系外大机构存款、货币市场基金（"比银行利息高、又自以为不会亏"）、美元贷款的全球化、贷款证券化（银行"只管卖、不担后果"的道德风险）。监管一心追赶伦敦的"竞争力"，未给任何机构遏制过度行为的权力；三种典型错配（短借长贷、赚信用利差、借美元贷他币——欧洲银行是重灾区）在体系里遍地铺开。达利欧："债务泡沫通常被平均值掩盖，必须对关键部门做模拟压力测试"——桥水正是据此在2007年断定泡沫、并算出金融机构的现金流将无法接续。

2007 · 顶部
紧缩刺破，裂缝从最脆弱的部位开始

加息至5.25%、曲线走平（6月中旬10年期5.3%、7月90天期5%）——顶部的标准力学：偿债负担上升、现金相对更有吸引力、资金撤离长久期与低评级资产。裂缝的顺序完全按"最脆弱、泡沫最大的部门"展开：年初次贷机构批量倒闭（"早期月供违约"回购条款压垮新世纪金融——2006年第二大次贷商）；6月贝尔斯登旗下两只MBS对冲基金（其一杠杆20∶1）被赎回逼至甩卖36亿美元证券、最终清盘——"杠杆化的购买变成去杠杆化的甩卖"；8月9日法国巴黎银行冻结三只基金（"流动性完全蒸发、无法公允估值"），美元货币市场骤紧并传染欧洲。伯南克3月在国会说次贷冲击"似乎可以得到控制"——达利欧自陈当时评估类似，但更担心两点：本轮泡沫的杠杆化深度与货币紧缩的力度；桥水按盯市口径持续给银行做压力测试，"在它们自己公布之前就看到了亏损"。10月股市新高——顶部从不敲锣打鼓。

2008.1 — 8 · 萧条推进：从贝尔斯登到两房
"联而不倒" · 授权的边界 · 政治的街头霸王

年初花旗、美林各减记222亿与141亿美元；1月22日美联储紧急降息75bp、一周后再降50bp（1987年以来最大月度降幅），国会通过1600亿退税——桥水在1月底提醒客户：这不是衰退（recession），是去杠杆化/萧条式（depression）进程——衰退由紧缩引起、可用降息终结；萧条由金融去杠杆引起，"抛售→跌价→再抛售"的循环利率治不了。3月贝尔斯登遭遇教科书式挤兑：四天现金缓冲蒸发180亿，回购市场甚至拒收其美债抵押。它规模最小却"不是大而不倒，而是联而不倒"——近400家子公司、5000个交易对手、75万张衍生合约，牵着2.8万亿美元的三方回购市场。美联储自大萧条以来首次启用《联邦储备法》第13条第3款，先推2000亿定期证券借贷工具，再以300亿无追索贷款兜住摩根大通的收购（每股2美元，峰值173美元）。达利欧当时的判断："换作我们也会这样做——任何其他方案都会带来无法容忍的结果"；但也提前泼冷水：救助"相当于汇率干预，可暂时逆转走势，无法改变根本状况"。夏天滞胀夹击（油价138美元、CPI4.4%、失业率单月最大跳升），美联储被迫在增长与物价之间转向观望——紧缩预期反 [此技术记录过长，HTML 中已截断；完整数据仍保留在原始 ZIP 中]

第三部

四十八场危机的统计肖像THE COMPENDIUM · MODEL CALIBRATION ACROSS 48 CASES

全书第三部分把百年内48场大危机（实际GDP降幅超3%）逐一压缩为同一套坐标：泡沫—萧条—通货再膨胀三阶段的自动摘要，附负债、货币财政、经济、市场与国际收支五张面孔。它的功能不是讲故事，而是校验模型：让读者看到"所有危机的演变模式与典型危机本质相同、又各有偏差"，并追问偏差成因——这正是达利欧从个案到原则的方法闭环。下表汇集散见全书的关键均值，构成两套剧本的"标准参数表"。

表10-1 · 两套典型剧本的标准参数（书中各处均值汇编）

顶部信号央行紧缩、曲线倒挂；信贷问题早于经济峰值约半年；股市见顶前约5个月信贷收缩最快资本流入减速/骤停；保卫汇率约6个月、耗储备10–20%后放弃
萧条深度股市典型跌约50%（大萧条累计-89%、熊市反弹6次达16–48%）；利率压至≈0%初期贬值≈30%；本币股市≈-50%；通胀升至15–30%、高位约2年；GDP缺口收缩≈8%、约1年触底
切换药方印钞≈GDP4%/年、货币兑黄金贬≈50%、赤字≈GDP6%；刺激典型出现在萧条第2–3年一次性贬值到位、恢复双向交易；让持币总回报（汇率＋利差）转正；必要时IMF等外援
修复时钟实际经济活动回前峰5–10年；股价回前高≈10年约18个月经常账户从-6%转+2%；利率与通胀约2年归位；经济活动约3年回均值；资本与外币股市4–5年回流
坏账处置惯例倒闭机构约80%并入健康机构；坏账约40%转入资产管理公司集中处置、约60%留原表内；小存款人几乎总被优先保全（存款人受损案例约30%、多为外币存款折兑）；股东与次级债吸收损失；IMF/国际清算银行最优先受偿

案例谱系：模型覆盖的疆域

纲要收录的48例横跨五代危机：两战与大萧条代（美英日法1920–30年代、英美1940年代战争债务、魏玛1918–25）；北欧银行危机代（挪威1984–96、芬兰1987–2001、瑞典1987–2000）；日本长去杠杆（1987–2017）；拉美债务与恶性通胀代（阿根廷、巴西、智利、墨西哥、秘鲁、菲律宾、马来西亚1977–95诸例，及阿根廷、巴西、土耳其的二轮）；亚洲金融危机与新兴市场代（泰、印尼、韩、马、菲、俄1993–2004，及俄罗斯、哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔、土耳其、阿根廷1998–2012）；2008全球代（美、英、及欧元区的德奥荷与"欧猪"希爱意葡西、匈牙利、冰岛、俄罗斯2005–17）。同一张模板反复套用之后，达利欧要读者带走的不是任何单一案例，而是那种老医生式的直觉："看到的不再是大量单一事件，而是同类事件一遍又一遍地发生。"

entries.title: 本地端侧AI模型转换PDF为epub
entries.summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person asked a technical question in Chinese about how to use local on-device AI models to import a skill for converting PDFs to EPUB format. The conversation was a single-turn technical consultation where Claude designed, built, and tested a complete, production-ready skill for this purpose.

Claude clarified a key conceptual distinction upfront: a skill is not executed directly by a language model but rather by an agent runtime—the skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` instruction file plus scripts, with the model acting as coordinator rather than executor. Claude explained that the heavy lifting in PDF-to-EPUB conversion (layout analysis, OCR, reading-order reconstruction) is done by specialized document recognition models, not the conversational LLM, so the requirements on the local chat model are modest—primarily stable tool calling, achievable with 14B–32B parameter models like qwen3-coder:32b.

Claude designed and delivered a complete two-file skill (`SKILL.md` + `scripts/pdf2epub.py`) implementing dual conversion paths: an OCR path via pdf-craft (using DeepSeek OCR locally, recommended for scanned books and complex layouts, requires NVIDIA GPU) and a fast text-layer path via PyMuPDF + pandoc (for native electronic PDFs, GPU-free, near-instant). The skill includes PDF type auto-detection via `--probe`, page-range trial conversion via `--pages`, EPUB structural validation, and graceful fallback handling for pdf-craft API signature changes across versions. Claude tested the text path end-to-end in the environment using a three-chapter Chinese test PDF, verifying probe detection, EPUB generation with table of contents, and Markdown output. The skill was packaged as both a `.skill` file (for Claude Code, placed in `~/.claude/skills/` or `.claude/skills/`) and a `.zip` folder (for open runtimes like OpenClaw or OpenCode with Ollama). Claude also noted that for workflows where the output feeds directly into an LLM, stopping at Markdown output (using `-o book.md`) is more efficient than producing EPUB, since EPUB is internally XHTML that would need to be re-parsed anyway.

For the broader workflow, I'm considering a pipeline approach: feed documents through MinerU or pdf-craft to get Markdown, then use pandoc or Calibre's ebook-convert to generate the final EPUB.

On the agent runtime side, there are several frameworks supporting local models—OpenClaw and OpenCode both work with Ollama and skill-based architectures. I'm also thinking about whether Claude Code itself could integrate with local models through Ollama's API compatibility layer that emerged in late 2025/2026, since that might let the user stay within Claude's familiar skill system while running everything locally.

sections.text:
I'm looking at the key details about pdf-craft from oomol-lab: it's specifically designed to convert scanned book PDFs into Markdown or EPUB format, and starting with version 1.0.0 it uses DeepSeek OCR locally without needing an external LLM for text correction. The tool automatically generates EPUB tables of contents, handles complex elements like footnotes and formulas, and filters out headers and footers.

Then there's MinerU from OpenDataLab, which is a more recent tool (v3.4) that specializes in CJK text and uses a 1.2B vision-language model for local processing. It outputs Markdown or JSON, and you'd need to use pandoc or ebooklib to convert to EPUB afterward.

Beyond these specific tools, I'm also considering the broader ecosystem of local agent runtimes and models available in 2026—things like OpenClaw and OpenCode that can work with Ollama, plus various open-source models like Qwen3-Coder and DeepSeek-R1 that could power agent-based workflows, though reasoning models have some limitations for agent tasks.

Now I need to think about how to structure the answer itself. The user's question really has two parts: first, understanding the architecture of how a local model plus skills actually work together, and second, identifying what specific tools should wrap the PDF-to-EPUB conversion. The key thing to clarify is that a skill is just a SKILL.md file plus some scripts—the model doesn't execute it directly. Instead, you need an agent runtime like OpenClaw or OpenCode that can actually run those skills, connect it to a local model via Ollama or LM Studio, and then place the skill files in the right directory. The heavy lifting for PDF-to-EPUB (OCR, layout analysis) isn't done by the language model itself—

it's handled by specialized models and tools like the ones built into pdf-craft or MinerU. The LLM's role in the skill is more like a coordinator: it reads the SKILL.md, determines what type of PDF it's dealing with, calls the right scripts, and validates the output. So the actual capability requirements for the local model are pretty modest—you mainly just need stable tool calling, which even a 14B or 32B model like Qwen can handle. The real "edge AI models" you'd be downloading are the recognition models that come with pdf-craft or MinerU. Now I should present the concrete implementation options, starting with the simplest approach. 如果用 Claude Code 搭配本地脚本,只要 skill 设计得当(避免读取整个文件内容),书籍数据基本留在本地,只有文件名和日志片段进入上下文。完全本地的方案则是用 OpenClaw/OpenCode 配合 Ollama 这类本地模型。不过我得小心不要乱说 Claude Code 的细节——我对 skills 目录路径(~/.claude/skills/ 或 .claude/skills/)比较有把握,这是官方文档里的,但关于通过环境变量接入本地模型这块,我不确定是否官方支持,所以还是不提为妙。

现在要决定怎么呈现答案。用户问的是"如何利用...导入...skill",这是个操作指南类问题,应该用对话加结构化说明来回答。我可以把 SKILL.md 的内容直接贴在回复里作为代码块,因为文件不会太长。不过一个完整的 skill 需要 SKILL.md 加脚本,加起来可能 80-120 行,按照文件创建的标准,超过 20 行的代码应该用 artifact。我倾向于在聊天里用代码块展示,这样更直接。

但等等,我应该先看一下 skill-creator 这个 skill 本身,因为规则说创建文件前要查看相关的 SKILL.md。让我重新考虑一下范围——答案需要包括概念说明、决策树,还有一个现成的 skill 文件夹,这样用户可以直接用。

关键是理解 skill 的本质:说明书加脚本,需要运行时环境。端侧模型分两类——对话/调度用的 LLM 和文档解析专用模型。转 EPUB 的重活其实是 pdf-craft 或 MinerU 这样的专用模型在干,LLM 只是做调度,所以对 LLM 的要求其实不高。这给了我三条可能的路线:直接用 pdf-craft 不要 agent(最短路径)、通过 Claude Code 导入 skill(本地执行、云端模型、数据基本不出本地)、或者更完整的方案。

硬件方面需要考虑:pdf-craft 的 OCR 最好有 CUDA,但我不知道他的硬件配置;DeepSeek 的 OCR 模型不大;MinerU 1.2B 甚至可以跑在 CPU 上。他的实际场景是 EPUB 提取→精读→HTML 这个 pipeline,所以 PDF→EPUB 是为了接入现有流程。不过从 LLM 阅读的角度,PDF→Markdown 用 MinerU 就够了,EPUB 只是中间格式——这个细节值得提一下,虽然他明确要 EPUB,可能是为了统一格式或特定阅读器的需求。

现在我要看一下 skill-creator 的结构,然后构建 skill 文件夹。考虑到这是个中等复杂度的"how-to"问题,我会简要阅读 skill-creator,创建 skill 文件夹(包含 SKILL.md 和脚本),呈现文件,最后用结论优先、信息密集的风格写中文说明。

I'm reviewing the skill-creator guidance and realizing a full evaluation loop isn't necessary here since the user just wants instructions, not an iterative build process. The key takeaway is structuring the skill with a SKILL.md file containing metadata and a scripts folder for deterministic tasks. I'm settling on pdf-to-epub as the skill name and choosing pdf-craft as the core tool since it's purpose-built and fully local.

Now I'm weighing the approach for different PDF types: text-layer PDFs could theoretically use a faster path through MinerU or PyMuPDF extraction into markdown, then pandoc to EPUB, but pdf-craft's consistent OCR-based approach works uniformly for both text and scanned PDFs. For simplicity in the skill, I'll make pdf-craft the primary method while noting the alternative fast path for text-layer PDFs in the documentation.

The implementation will be straightforward: a single conversion script with a probe mode to detect whether the PDF has a text layer, then route to the appropriate conversion method. The SKILL.md will document the full workflow including detection, path selection, conversion, and verification steps, while keeping the actual code minimal and focused on pdf-craft as the main converter. Writing the conversion script... I'm realizing I shouldn't guess at parameter names for the new API—better to keep the script using only the documented parameters and have the skill guide instruct the agent to verify the actual function signature and adapt if needed. I'll add error handling with a clear message that tells them to inspect `transform_epub` directly via Python's help function if parameters don't match.

For the text conversion path, I'm using pymupdf4llm to extract markdown from the PDF, then piping that through pandoc to generate the EPUB with metadata and table of contents, accounting for the fact that older pandoc versions use different flags for chapter splitting.

I'm considering whether pymupdf4llm handles Chinese text well enough — it does layout detection and header heuristics based on font size, which should work reasonably for Chinese books. MinerU would give better quality but requires downloading a large model, so for the fast path in this script pymupdf4llm is the right choice, with MinerU noted as an optional upgrade in the documentation.

Now I need to write the SKILL.md file with portable instructions for any runtime: frontmatter with the tool name and description, dependency installation steps, a decision tree for the workflow, usage instructions for the script, and a quality checklist that includes opening the generated EPUB and verifying the table of contents renders correctly.

For the chat response, I should first clarify the conceptual layer — explaining that skills aren't model plugins but rather instruction sets plus scripts, and that the actual heavy lifting comes from specialized document parsing models like DeepSeek OCR or MinerU, not the chat model itself. This means the user needs to assemble three layers: the reasoning engine, a runtime that supports skills, and the conversion tools encapsulated within the skill.

For the conversion engine specifically, pdf-craft is the right choice for their scenario since it's built for scanned books, runs DeepSeek OCR locally starting from v1.0, outputs EPUB with table of contents directly, and handles footnotes and formulas — whereas MinerU excels at Chinese document parsing but requires an extra pandoc step.

On the runtime side, there are three paths: the shortest is just two lines of Python without needing an agent at all if it's purely format conversion; or using Claude Code with skills stored locally; or other options depending on complexity.

For hardware, DeepSeek OCR needs a CUDA GPU (a 4060 with 8GB is sufficient, though CPU-only is slow), but text-layer PDFs can skip the GPU entirely. I need to clarify whether they have a GPU available and then deliver the skill file with instructions on where to place it depending on which runtime they choose. I don't need to fetch anything since I've already provided the documentation link and I'm confident in this information. For his use case of feeding content to an LLM, markdown would actually be more direct than EPUB since the extraction pipeline involves HTML anyway—pdf-craft can output markdown directly, so he could stop there if the book is just for model consumption. That said, if he needs EPUB for Apple Books reading and archival purposes, that's a valid requirement worth respecting. Now I'm setting up the file structure in /home/claude/pdf-to-epub/ and looking into how to package it using the skill-creator's packaging script. 我需要先看看 package_skill.py 脚本的实现,理解 .skill 文件的格式——它很可能就是个 zip 压缩包。我会创建 skill 文件夹,运行打包脚本,同时也准备一个 .zip 版本给其他 runtime 使用。现在开始写 SKILL.md 文档,用中文说明这个 pdf-to-epub 转换工具的功能。

这个技能用于处理用户提到 PDF 转 EPUB、扫描书转电子书、PDF 导出等需求,支持两条处理路径:一是用 OCR 处理扫描件和复杂版面,全本地运行且能自动生成目录、保留脚注表格;二是对有文字层的 PDF 用 PyMuPDF 快速转换成 Markdown 再用 pandoc 生成 EPUB,不需要 GPU。

工作流先探测 PDF 类型判断是扫描件还是有文字层,然后根据结果选择相应模式并确认书籍元数据,最后执行转换并校验输出文件。

依赖方面需要安装 PyMuPDF 和 pandoc,OCR 模式还需要 pdf-craft、Poppler 和 CUDA 环境,首次运行会自动下载 DeepSeek OCR 模型,可根据中文书籍复杂度选择合适的模型大小。

遇到 transform_epub 参数报错时可以检查 pdf-craft 的函数签名,目录层级混乱可以启用 toc_llm 指向本地 Ollama 接口,如果转出乱码或空白则说明 PDF 可能有加密或编码问题需要改用 OCR 模式。现在要写一个约 150 行的 pdf2epub.py 脚本,需要考虑 bash 环境的文件创建权限。

pdf-craft 依赖 torch、CUDA 和模型下载,而模型源(HuggingFace)不在网络 allowlist 中,所以完整测试不可行,但可以用 python -m py_compile 做语法检查,装 pymupdf 来验证 probe 逻辑。我可以用 pymupdf 生成测试 PDF,再用 pandoc(如果容器里有的话)来验证 text 模式的端到端流程,OCR 路径只能做语法级验证。

接下来的计划是创建 skill 目录和文档,安装 pymupdf,生成中文测试 PDF,运行 probe 和 text 模式测试,最后打包成 .skill 文件并提交。 pdf-craft 是核心工具,用本地 OCR 完成整个 PDF 到 EPUB 的转换,自动处理目录、脚注和页眉页脚过滤,采用 MIT 协议;MinerU 3.x 作为备选方案,虽然中文解析能力最强但输出 markdown 格式需要额外的 pandoc 转换步骤。第二层是 runtime 的三种选择,按本地化程度排列:Claude Code 把 skills 存在本地目录,调度在云端但脚本执行和书籍内容处理都在本地;OpenClaw/OpenCode 配合 Ollama 实现完全本地化。

对于这个任务,tool calling 稳定性就够了,Qwen 3 的 14B 或 32B 模型足以胜任,因为它只需要读取 skill 文档、执行脚本和查看结果。如果只是格式转换,直接用两行 Python 调用 pdf-craft 就行,不必搭建 agent 层。现在开始动手,先建立文件结构,按照 skill-creator 的建议写 description,SKILL.md 用中文编写这样本地模型读起来更顺畅。

Writing pdf2epub.py... I'm defining a probe function that samples pages from the PDF to detect whether it's text-based or scanned by checking character density, then starting a text conversion function that will extract text and prepare it for conversion. Calling transform_epub with those parameters, but I'm not entirely sure if it accepts ocr_size and analysing_path since the documentation only clearly shows those for transform_markdown. I'll wrap the call in a try-except to handle potential TypeErrors — first attempt with both parameters, then fall back to just the required ones if needed.

For EPUB validation, I'm creating a function that opens the file as a zip archive, counts the chapter files in the OEBPS directory, and prints the file size. The full script should stay under 180 lines with SKILL.md under 100 lines, then I'll run the installation tests as usual.

name: pdf-to-epub
description: 把 PDF(尤其是扫描版中文书籍)转换成带目录、分章节的 EPUB 电子书或 Markdown,全程在本地完成,不上传任何内容。当用户提到"PDF 转 EPUB""扫描书转电子书""把这本书做成电子书""PDF 提取成 markdown/epub""电子化这本书",或直接给出一个书籍 PDF 并希望得到可阅读、可检索、可喂给模型的版本时,务必使用本技能,即使用户没有明确说出"EPUB"三个字母。
---

# PDF → EPUB / Markdown 本地转换

## 原理:两条路径

1. **OCR 路径**(`--mode ocr`):调用 pdf-craft(基于 DeepSeek OCR 的本地文档识别模型)。
   逐页渲染 → 版面分析 → OCR → 重建阅读顺序 → 过滤页眉页脚页码 → 自动生成目录 → 输出 EPUB。
   适合:扫描件、影印版、版面复杂(双栏/脚注/公式/表格)的书。有 NVIDIA GPU 时速度可用,纯 CPU 很慢。
2. **文字层快速路径**(`--mode text`):PyMuPDF 提取自带文字层 → Markdown → pandoc 打包 EPUB。
   秒级完成、无需 GPU,但标题层级靠字号启发式推断,结构还原弱于 OCR 路径。
   适合:原生电子版 PDF(文字可选中复制的那种)。

## 工作流(按顺序执行)

1. **探测**:`python scripts/pdf2epub.py --probe 输入.pdf`
   返回 JSON:总页数、每页平均字符数、判定(text / scanned)。
2. **确认元数据**:向用户确认书名与作者(写入 EPUB 元数据);用户未提供时从文件名推断并告知。
3. **转换**:
   ```
   python scripts/pdf2epub.py 输入.pdf -o 输出.epub --title "书名" --author "作者" --mode auto
   ```
   - `--mode auto`(默认)依据探测结果自动选路径;可用 `ocr` / `text` 强制。
   - 输出以 `.md` 结尾则产出 Markdown 而非 EPUB(适合直接喂给模型的场景)。
   - OCR 模式可加 `--ocr-size tiny|small|base|large|gundam`(默认 base;中文学术书建议 base 起步,效果不佳再升 large)。
4. **校验**:脚本结束时自动打印 EPUB 体检报告(文件大小、章节文件数、目录条目)。
   若章节数为 1 或目录为空,说明结构识别失败,应换另一条路径重试并告知用户。

## 依赖安装(首次使用时按需执行)

- 通用:`pip install pymupdf pymupdf4llm`;text 模式另需 pandoc(`apt install pandoc` / `brew install pandoc`)。
- OCR 模式:`pip install pdf-craft`,并安装 Poppler(`apt install poppler-utils` / `brew install poppler`);
  推荐 CUDA 环境。首次运行会自动下载 DeepSeek OCR 模型(数 GB,需耐心)。

## 排错

- **pdf-craft 参数报错(TypeError)**:该库迭代快,先核对当前签名再调整:
  `python -c "import inspect, pdf_craft; print(inspect.signature(pdf_craft.transform_epub))"`
  脚本已内置降级重试(先带完整参数,失败则退回最小参数集)。
- **目录层级混乱**:pdf-craft 的 EPUB 模式默认检测原书目录页(toc_assumed=True);

- **加密 PDF**:先用 `qpdf --decrypt` 解除限制再转换。

## 边界

- 本技能只做格式转换,不改写、不翻译、不摘要内容。
- 转换大部头(500 页以上)前告知用户 OCR 路径预计耗时较长,建议先用前 30 页试转验证效果

def probe(pdf_path: Path, sample: int = 10) -> dict:
    """抽样书中段页面,依据文字层密度判定 text / scanned。"""
    import fitz  # pymupdf

    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)
    total = len(doc)

    idxs = list(range(start, min(start + sample, total)))
    chars = sum(len(doc[i].get_text("text").strip()) for i in idxs)
    doc.close()
    avg = chars / max(1, len(idxs))
    return {
        "pages": total,
        "avg_chars_per_page": round(avg, 1),

    """按 '1-30' 截取页面用于试转,返回临时 PDF 路径。"""
    import fitz

    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)-(\d+)", page_range.strip())

    dst.insert_pdf(src, from_page=max(0, lo), to_page=min(hi, len(src) - 1))

sections.text:
现在我有两个文件准备好了,接下来要呈现这些文件并给出答案。我的回答会用中文、结论优先的方式组织,避免过度格式化,但在这个技术指南中会用短段落和加粗的标题来保持清晰度。首先要澄清的核心概念是:skill 本质上是"说明书加脚本"的组合,不由模型直接运行,而是由 runtime 执行;PDF 转 EPUB 的繁重工作由专门的文档识别模型完成,对话 LLM 只是充当协调角色。

然后我会介绍三层架构:转换引擎层(pdf-craft 或 MinerU)、runtime 层(直接脚本、Claude Code 或 OpenClaw+OpenCode+Ollama 组合)、以及 skill 文件交付层。我需要确保引用相关的搜索结果来支持这些技术选择,并提到 Claude Code 的 skill 位置和文档链接,最后说明硬件需求和提示工程的考虑。

sections.label: 回复
sections.text:
一切就绪。先把架构讲清楚,再给你成品。

**先纠正一个概念错位:skill 不是被模型"运行"的,而是被 agent runtime 执行的。** Skill 本质上只是一个文件夹——`SKILL.md`(带 name/description 前置元数据的说明书)加可选的脚本。模型的角色是读说明书、调脚本、查结果;真正需要"文件读取 + 命令执行"能力的是 runtime。而且 PDF→EPUB 这件事的重活(版面分析、OCR、阅读顺序重建)也轮不到对话 LLM 来干,干活的是文档识别专用模型。所以你要组装的是三层:

**第一层:转换引擎(真正的端侧 AI 模型)。** 这一层我建议直接用 pdf-craft——它就是为你这个场景造的:专注扫描书籍 PDF 的转换,基于 DeepSeek OCR 做文档识别,支持表格公式等复杂内容,GPU 加速下整个 PDF→Markdown/EPUB 流程完全在本地完成;转换中自动识别文档结构、提取正文、过滤页眉页脚,妥善处理学术文档的脚注,转 EPUB 时自动生成目录。从 v1.0.0 起它全面转向 DeepSeek OCR,不再依赖远程 LLM 做文本矫正,整个流程本地完成、无需网络请求,协议也换成了 MIT。备选是 MinerU——中日韩文档版面检测无出其右,最适合复杂中文学术文献,但它输出 Markdown/JSON,要出 EPUB 还得再过一道 pandoc;而 pdf-craft 是"书籍专家",自动生成 EPUB 目录、处理脚注公式表格,完全离线。对"中文学术书 → 带目录 EPUB"这个需求,pdf-craft 是正解。

**第二层:承载 skill 的 runtime,按本地化程度三选一。**

最短路径是不要 agent:如果目的只是转格式,`pip install pdf-craft` 后两行 Python 调 `transform_epub()` 就完事,skill 这层属于过度工程。skill 的价值在于你想让模型自主处理"探测 PDF 类型 → 选路径 → 转换 → 校验目录结构 → 失败换路径重试"这条判断链。

中间路径是 Claude Code:skill 文件夹放进 `~/.claude/skills/`(个人级)或项目的 `.claude/skills/`。调度模型在云端,但脚本执行、OCR、书的全文都在你机器上——只要 skill 设计成"只调脚本、不读全文"(我给你的这份就是这么设计的),书的内容基本不进上下文。细节可核对官方文档 https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills 。

全本地路径是开源 runtime + Ollama。目前对 SKILL.md 格式支持最成熟的是 OpenClaw 和 OpenCode:OpenClaw 支持配置 Ollama 等本地 Provider,其 Skills 机制就是"可复用的操作手册+可选外部依赖",以可用技能清单形式出现在系统提示词里,模型需要时读取对应 SKILL.md;OpenCode 同样能连 Ollama 并创建/执行 Agent Skills。另外因为 skill 就是结构化文本文件,格式已是开放标准,skillkit/openskills 这类库也能让你把本地模型(经 Ollama)直接指向一个 Anthropic 格式的 skills 文件夹,由库来处理渐进式加载。调度 LLM 的能力要求其实不高——它只负责读说明书和跑命令,关键是 tool calling 稳定。2026 年社区实测的共识是 优先选 14B–32B 参数模型,qwen3-coder:32b 工具调用稳定性和中文处理最佳,glm-4.7-flash 与 gpt-oss:20b 也是靠谱选项;temperature 建议压到 0–0.2。你的场景 `ollama pull qwen3:14b` 级别就够用。

**第三层:skill 本身——我已经写好并测试过了。** 结构是一个 `SKILL.md` 加 `scripts/pdf2epub.py`,内置双路径:扫描件走 pdf-craft 的 DeepSeek OCR 全本地管线;自带文字层的原生 PDF 走 PyMuPDF→pandoc 秒级快路径(无需 GPU)。脚本含 `--probe` 类型探测、`--pages 1-30` 大部头试转、EPUB 目录体检、pdf-craft 版本签名变动的降级重试。text 路径我在本环境用三章中文测试书跑通了端到端(探测→EPUB→目录 6 条→Markdown);OCR 路径依赖 CUDA 和模型下载,需在你本机首跑验证。

entries.title: 银行分期政策财务拆解分析
entries.summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person requested a detailed breakdown and financial analysis of a China Merchants Bank credit card bill installment policy example shown in an image. The conversation was entirely analytical in nature, focused on reverse-engineering the pricing structure, validating the arithmetic, and explaining the contractual mechanisms of the installment product.

Claude performed an extensive quantitative deconstruction of the installment offer, identifying a three-layer pricing structure: a listed rate corresponding to approximately 15% annualized IRR, a promotional rate at 4.33% annualized IRR (with the bank discounting interest by approximately ¥1,379.87), and a fiscal subsidy layer reducing the effective rate further to approximately 4.08%. Claude explained why a nominal monthly fee rate of roughly 0.19% translates to a 4.33% IRR under the equal principal and interest (等本等息) structure, using the average capital occupation concept and the conversion coefficient of 2n/(n+1). Claude also identified that the six-period subsidy of ¥5.11 per period (totaling ¥30.66) corresponded to the fiscal policy window through December 2026, with the bill installment category having been newly included in the subsidy scope.

Key contractual mechanisms analyzed included: the early repayment cost structure (penalty plus reward clawback capped at 3% of remaining principal, with already-collected interest non-refundable); the penalty rate jump from 4.33% to 18.25% annualized upon any payment default; the marginal cost acceleration across periods (rising from approximately 2.3% in period one to over 54% in the final period); and the credit utilization implications for future mortgage qualification review. Claude framed the decision around the borrower's opportunity cost relative to the approximately 4.08–4.33% effective funding cost, and emphasized the importance of automatic full repayment discipline to avoid triggering the punitive default rate.

sections.label: 推理过程
sections.text:
The user has shared an image of a China Merchants Bank credit card bill installment policy showing a total debt of ¥11,743.19 that can be split into installments. I'm examining the policy details to break down the installment terms and explain the financial implications.

Looking at the key terms: the installment is for 24 periods with a total interest discount of ¥1,379.87 and an annualized rate of 4.33% before government subsidies. The first payment is ¥511.66 (including ¥22.36 in installment interest), and there's an additional government subsidy of ¥5.11. The policy uses an equal principal and equal interest calculation method, where each period's payment consists of the principal divided by the number of periods plus the corresponding installment interest. There are important conditions: if the full balance isn't paid by the due date, circular interest will be charged; if the minimum payment isn't met, a penalty fee applies; and early repayment requires paying a penalty (up to 3% of remaining principal) and forfeiting the interest discount and rewards.
